10:1: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed on that. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: I am God, I see. Who said that? Yahya bin Dawud bin Maimun Al-Wasiti told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Alif, Lam, Ra, I am God, I see. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Alif Lam Ra, he said: I am God, I see. Others said: They are letters from the name of God, which is the Most Gracious. Who said that? Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwayh told me, he said, Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alif Lam Ra, “Ha Meem,” and Nun, the letters of Al-Rahman are disconnected. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Isa bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Othman, who said: Salim bin Abdullah mentioned Al-Ra, “Ha-Mim,” and Nun, and he said: The name Al-Rahman is disconnected, then he said: Al-Rahman. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Mandal told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: Alif-Lam-Ra, “Ha-Mim,” and Nun are the names of the Most Gracious. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr Al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Ismail bin Salem, on the authority of Amer: that he was asked about Alif Lam Ra, “Ha Meem,” and Sad. He said: They are names of God’s names that are separated by the alphabet, so if you connect them, they are names of God’s names. Others said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Alif Lam Ra is one of the names of the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among the people, and what each speaker has adopted in what he has said about it, and what is correct for us to say about it in its counterpart, and that is at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. We have only mentioned in this place the amount that we have mentioned, because the one whose statement we have mentioned in this contradicts his statement in (Alif, Lam, Meem.) As for those who reconciled the meanings of all of that, we have mentioned their statement there, and it is sufficient not to repeat it here. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: These are the verses of the wise Book. Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Those are verses from the Torah. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid: These are the verses of the Wise Book, he said: the Torah and the Gospel.... He said, Ishaq told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: These are the verses of the Book, he said: the books that came before the Qur’an. Others said: The meaning of this is: These are the verses of the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as: These are the verses of the Qur’an, and directed the meaning of those to the meaning of these. We have explained the direction of directing those to this meaning in Surat al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And the verses, the flags, and the Book, is one of the names of the Qur’an, and we have explained all of that previously. We said: This interpretation is more correct in this regard, because the Torah and the Gospel were not mentioned before, nor were they recited after, so the report could be directed to them. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement: And the Most Gracious, these are the verses of the Wise Qur’an. The meaning of the wise in this context is the decisive. “Maf’al” was changed to Fa’il, just as it was said: A painful torment, meaning painful, and as the poet said: Rayhana's security is the all-hearing supplicant We have explained this in more than one place in the book. Its meaning, then, is: These are the verses of the perfect Book, which God perfected and explained to His servants, as He, the Most High, said: “Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book whose verses have been perfected and then presented in detail from One Who is Wise and Acquainted” (Hud 11:1).
10:2: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Was it a wonder to the people that We revealed the Qur’an to a man among them, warning them of God’s punishment for their disobedience, as if they did not know that God had revealed before him to a human like him, so they were amazed at Our revelation to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saad told us, he said, Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When God sent Muhammad as a Messenger, the Arabs, or those among them who denied it, denied it, and said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human being like Muhammad! So God Almighty revealed: Is it a wonder to mankind that We have revealed to a man from among them? And He said: And We did not send before you except men (Yusuf 12:109). Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Quraysh were amazed that a man from among them was sent. He said: And similar to that: And to Aad [We sent] their brother Hud (al-A’raf 7:65), And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih (al-A’raf 7:73), God said: Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you (al-A’raf 7:69). The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Was it not a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: Warn the people, and give good tidings to those who believe in God and His Messenger: that they will have a sure footing is in apposition to warn. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: He came forward truthfully. Some of them said: It means that they will have a good reward for the good deeds they have done. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: They will have a position of truth with their Lord, he said: A reward of truth.... He said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid: They will have a position of truth with their Lord, he said: righteous deeds. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord, meaning: a good reward for the deeds they have done. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Abdullah bin Abi Mugheeth, on the authority of Mujahid: They will have a position of truth with their Lord, he said: their prayers, their fasting, their charity, and their glorification of God. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A true gift, he said: good. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He came forward truthfully, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.... He said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, who said: A true gift, a true reward, is with their Lord. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, the same. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing, he said: The sure footing, the reward for the truth is what they have done of deeds. Others said: Its meaning is that they have a previous truth in the Preserved Tablet, from happiness. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord, he says: Happiness preceded them in the first mention. Others said: The meaning of this is that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is their intercessor, and he has spoken the truth. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Amr bin Al-Jun, on the authority of Qatada - or Al-Hasan - that they will have a position of truth with their Lord, he said: Muhammad is an intercessor for them. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord, meaning: a sure footing with their Lord. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, regarding his statement: They will have a sure footing with their Lord, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is that they have righteous deeds with God, for which they deserve reward from Him. It is said about the Arabs: These are the people of precedence in Islam, meaning: these are those who have done good in it, so they have precedence in it. And it is said: He has a true precedence with me, and a bad precedence, and that is what he has done of good or evil, and from this is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit: We have the upper hand over you, and we swear to our first in obedience to God. And the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: You have a foot that people do not deny that, with normal calculations, it has floated on the sea. Abu Jaafar said: The interpretation of the statement is: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a reward better than righteous deeds with their Lord. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: The disbelievers said, ‘This is indeed an obvious magician.’ Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed. So the people of Medina and Basra generally read it as: This is clear magic, meaning: What you have brought to us - meaning the Qur’an - is clear magic. Masruq, Saeed bin Jubair, and a group of Kufi readers read it as: This is indeed a clear magician. I have previously explained similar examples of this: that every thing described with a description, the described indicates its description, and its description indicates it. The reader has a choice in reading in this regard, and that is similar to this letter: (The disbelievers said, This is indeed clear magic), and A clear magician. That is because they described him as a magician, and their description of what he brought them as magic, indicates that they described it as magic. Since that is the case, then it is the same whichever of these the reader reads, because the meaning of the two readings is the same. There is something omitted in the speech, and the indication of what was mentioned was sufficient for what was left out, which is: (So when he gave them good tidings, he warned them and recited to them the revelation), the disbelievers said: Indeed, what he has brought to us is obvious magic. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement then is: Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: Warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord? But when he brought them the revelation of God and recited it to them, those who denied the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger said: This that Muhammad has brought to us is obvious magic, meaning: He makes it clear to you that what he claims is false.
10:3: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Your Lord, to whom all things are due worship, and none is worthy of worship except Him, is the One who created the seven heavens and the seven earths in six days, and He alone created them without a partner or supporter, then He rose over His throne, managing affairs, judging in His creation as He wills, no one opposes Him in His judgment, no one follows His management, and no defect enters His affairs, There is no intercessor except after His permission, meaning: no intercessor will intercede with Him on the Day of Resurrection for anyone, except after He gives permission for intercession, That is God, your Lord, meaning: This One whose description is like this, is your Master and your Lord, not one of the gods and idols who does not hear, see, manage, or judge. So worship Him, meaning: So worship your Lord whose description is like this, and devote worship to Him, and single out for Him divinity and lordship, with humility. From you to Him, without your idols and everything else that you associate with Him in worship, Will you not remember? He says: Will you not learn a lesson and take heed from these verses and arguments, so that you may return to submitting to the oneness of your Lord and singling Him out for worship, and renounce rivals and disavow them? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He manages the matter, he said: He decides it alone. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: He manages the affair, and there is no intercessor except after His permission, he said: He decides it alone. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He manages the matter, he said: He decides it alone.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
10:4: Abu Ja`far said: The Most High says: To your Lord, whose description is what He, the Most High, described in the verse before this, is your return, O people, on the Day of Resurrection, all of you, the promise of God is true. So He made the promise of God a source from His statement: To Him is your return, because it contains the meaning of (the promise), and its meaning is: God promises you that He will revive you after your death, a true promise. Therefore, He made the promise of God is true in the accusative case. He begins creation, then He will repeat it. The Most High says: Your Lord begins the creation, its occurrence, and its existence, then He will repeat it. He says: Then He will repeat it and find it alive as it was on the day He began it, after its annihilation and its affliction, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He begins creation and then repeats it, he said: He brings it to life and then causes it to die. Abu Ja`far said: And I think he said: (Then He brings it to life). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid: He begins creation and then repeats it, he said: He brings it to life, then causes it to die, then brings it to life. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He begins creation and then repeats it, he brings it to life, then causes it to die, then he begins it, then brings it to life.... He said, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Warqa`, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. The reading of the regions is: Indeed, He begins creation, with a kasra on the alif of indeed, as a resumption. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Jaafar al-Razi that he read it, that he, with the opening of the alif from that he anhu. As if he meant: Truly, He begins creation and then repeats it, so that then becomes a nominative, as the poet said: Is it true, servants of God, that I am not a visitor to my Lord’s Paradise except that I am watched? And His statement: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice, meaning: Then He will return him after his death to the state he was in before his death when he is resurrected from his grave. That He may reward those who believe, meaning: To reward those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God commanded them to do of deeds, and avoided what He forbade them from doing, for their good deeds, with justice, meaning: To reward them for the good deeds they did in this world with good reward and righteous recompense in the Hereafter. And that is justice, and justice is justice and fairness, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With justice, with fairness. His saying: And those who disbelieve will have a drink of scalding water, for He, the Most High, began the report of what God has prepared for those who disbelieve of punishment, and in the sense of a conjunction with the first. Because He, the Most High, mentioned the report of the return of all of them, their disbelievers and their believers, to Him. Then He informed of their protection so that He might reward each group for what they lived, the good among them for good, and the evil for evil. But since the renewed report of what has been prepared for those who disbelieve of punishment had already been presented, indicating to the listener what was intended, He began the report, and the meaning is a conjunction, and said: And those who denied God and His Messenger and belied the signs of God, for them is a drink in Hell of scalding water, and that is a drink that has been boiled and its heat has become intense, so that according to what was mentioned about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it drips from one of them when he brings it close to the scalp, and as He, the Most High, described it: Like molten metal, scalding the faces (al-Kahf 18:29). Its origin is: (maf`ul), which was changed to (fa`il), but it is (mahmum), meaning heated. And everything heated among the Arabs is (hameem), and from it is the saying of Al-Muraqqash: And every day she has a still, in which there is a well of boiling water and boiling water. By hot water means heated water. And His saying: A painful punishment, means: And for them, in addition to that, is a painful punishment, in addition to drinking scalding water, because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger.
10:5: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Your Lord is God who created the heavens and the earth, It is He who made the sun a radiance, during the day, and the moon a light, at night. The meaning of that is: He is the One who illuminated the sun and lit up the moon, and determined for it phases, meaning: He decreed for it and made it phases, which it does not exceed or fall short of, in one state forever. He said: And its measure is mansions, so he made it unique, and he mentioned the sun and the moon, so there are two aspects to that: One of them: that the ha in his saying: and His measure refers specifically to the moon, because the passing of months and years is known by the crescent moons, not by the sun. The other: that he was satisfied with mentioning one of them over the other, as he said in another place: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should be pleased (al-Tawbah 9:62), and as the poet said: He threw me into a matter that my father and I were innocent of, and he threw me into a deep hole And His statement: That you may know the number of years and the reckoning, meaning: And the measure of that in stages, that you may know, you people, the number of years, the entry of what enters from them, or the expiration of what is to come from them, and their reckoning, meaning: and the reckoning of the times of the years, and the number of their days, and the reckoning of the hours of their days, God did not create that except in truth, meaning: He, the Most High, says: God did not create the sun and the moon and their stages except in truth. The Truth, the Most High, says: He says: All of that is in truth alone, without help or partner, He details the verses, meaning: He clarifies the arguments and proofs, for a people who know, if they ponder them, the truth of the Oneness of God, and the truth of what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls them to, of rejecting rivals and disavowing idols.
10:6: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, alerting His servants to the place of evidence of His Lordship, and that He is the Creator of everything below Him: Indeed, in the succession of night to day, and the succession of day to night, when this goes, this comes, and when this comes, this goes, and in what God created in the heavens of the sun, moon, and stars, and in the earth of the wonders of creation indicating that they have a Creator like none other, are signs, meaning: clear proofs, arguments, and signs, for a people who fear God, so they fear His threat, and dread His punishment for sincerely worshipping their Lord. If someone says: First, is there any evidence in what God created in the heavens and the earth of its Creator except for those who fear God? It was said: In that is clear evidence of its Creator for everyone whose nature is sound and whose heart is free from defects. And the report was not intended to indicate that it is evidence for whoever has made his soul feel fear of God, but rather its meaning is: Indeed in that are signs for whoever fears God’s punishment, and his desires do not lead him to go against what is clear to him of the truth, because that indicates to everyone with a sound nature that he has a Manager who deserves to be worshipped, not anyone else of gods and rivals.
10:7: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Those who do not fear meeting Us on the Day of Resurrection are therefore deniers of reward and punishment, competing in the adornments and decorations of this world, satisfied with it in exchange for the Hereafter, reassured and at ease with it. And those who are heedless of the signs of God - which are His proofs of His Oneness and His arguments for His servants in the sincerity of worship to Him - are turning away from them and distracted, not contemplating them with the contemplation of a sincere person, so that they may know through them the truth of what they have guided them to, and they may know through them the length of time they have been residing in them.
10:8: Their abode is the Fire, God Almighty says: Those who have this description, their abode, their destiny is the Fire of Hell in the Hereafter, because of what they used to earn, in this world of sins and crimes, and the evil deeds they committed. The Arabs say: So-and-so does not fear so-and-so, if he does not fear him. From this is the saying of God Almighty: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? (Nuh: 13), and from this is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it and he stays in a house full of honey bees. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they are content with it, he said: It is like His saying: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We fully repay them for their deeds therein (Hud 11:15). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure in it, he said: It is like his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein (Hud 11:15). Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement, Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs, he said: If you wish, you will see a worldly person who rejoices in it, is saddened by it, is angry with it, and is pleased with it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure in it, the entire verse, he said: These are the people of disbelief. Then he said: Those - their refuge is the Fire for what they used to earn.
10:9: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, that is, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and done righteous deeds, that is, the work of obeying God and adhering to His command, their Lord will guide them by their faith, that is, their Lord will guide them by their faith in Him, to Paradise as: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in Gardens of Delight.” It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a believer emerges from his grave, his deeds will be presented to him in a beautiful form, and he will say to him: Who are you? By God, I see you are a man of truth! He will say: I am your deeds! So it will be a light and a guide for him to Paradise. As for the disbeliever, when he emerges from his grave, his deeds will be presented to him in a bad form and a bad sign, and he will say: Who are you? By God, I see you are a bad man! He will say: I am your deeds! So he will be taken away until he enters the Fire.” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Their Lord guides them by their faith, he said: It will be a light for them by which they walk. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.... He said, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Warqa`, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said: Their Lord will guide them by their faith, he said: His deeds will be presented to him in a beautiful form and a pleasant smell, and he will confront his companion and give him good report of every good thing, and he will say to him: Who are you? He will say: I am your deeds! Then He will make a light for him from before him until he enters Paradise. That is His statement: Their Lord will guide them by their faith. As for the disbeliever, his deeds will be presented to him in a bad form and a foul smell, and he will stick to his companion and cling to him until he throws him into the Fire. Others said: The meaning of this is: By their faith, their Lord guides them to His religion. He says: By their belief, He guided them. Who said that?.... And His statement: Rivers flow beneath them, means: Rivers of Paradise flow beneath these believers, whose description God Almighty has described. In gardens of pleasure, means: in orchards of pleasure, with which God has blessed the people of His obedience and faith in Him. If someone were to say: How is it said: Rivers flow beneath them, when God Almighty described the rivers of Paradise throughout the Qur’an as flowing beneath the gardens? How can rivers flow beneath them, unless they are above ground and rivers flow beneath the ground? And this is not a description of the rivers of Paradise, because their description is that they flow on the surface of the earth, not in trenches? It was said: The meaning of that is different from what you have said, but rather the meaning of that is: the rivers flow from below them to what is before them in the gardens of bliss, and that is similar to the statement of God: Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream (Maryam 19:24). And it is known that He did not place the stream beneath it while it was a base on it - since the stream is the canal - but rather He meant by it: He placed it below it in front of it, and as God, the Most High, said, informing about what Pharaoh said: Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? (al-Zukhruf 43:51), meaning: below me, in front of me.
10:10: As for his saying: “Their supplication therein is: Glory be to You, O God,” its meaning is: Their supplication therein is: Glory be to You, O God, as: - Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed of His statement: “Their prayer therein will be: ‘Glory be to You, O God.’” He said: When a bird passes by them, they desire it, they say: Glory be to You, O God. And that is their prayer. Then the angel brings them what they desire, and greets them, and they respond to him. That is His statement: “And their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” He said: Then when they eat, they praise God, their Lord. That is His statement: “And the final prayer of theirs will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Their call therein will be: Glory be to You, O God,” meaning: That is what they will say therein, “and their greeting therein will be: Peace.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ubayd God al-Ashja’i told us, he said, I heard Sufyan say: “Their supplication therein is: Glory be to You, O God, and their greeting therein is: Peace.” He said: When they want something, they say: O God, and what they supplicated for comes to them. As for his saying: Glory be to You, O God, its meaning is: To glorify You, O Lord, from what the polytheists have attributed to You, of lying and slander against You. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, I heard my father, on the authority of more than one person, Atiyah among them: (Glory be to God), glorifying God. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Muhab, he said: I heard Musa bin Talha say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ‘Glory be to God.’ He said: ‘God’s absolution from evil.’” Abu Kuraib, Abu Al-Sa’ib, and Khallad bin Aslam told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Qabus told us, on the authority of his father: Ibn Al-Kawwa asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about Glory be to God. He said: It is a word that God is pleased with for Himself. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Saeed Al-Thawri, on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Muhab Al-Talhi, on the authority of Musa bin Talha, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ‘Glory be to God,’ and he said: ‘To sanctify God from evil.’” Ali bin Isa Al-Bazzar told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Hammad told us, he said, Hafs bin Sulaiman told us, he said, Talha bin Yahya bin Talha told us, on the authority of his father, “on the authority of Talha bin Ubaidullah, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the interpretation of “Glory be to God,” and he said: It is the purification of God from all evil.” Muhammad bin Amr bin Tamam Al-Kalbi told me, he said, Sulayman bin Ayoub told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Musa bin Talha, on the authority of his father, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, what about saying Glory be to God? He said: It is to sanctify God from evil. And their greeting, he says: and their greeting to one another, “is peace,” meaning: I was safe and secure from what the people of Hell were afflicted with. The Arabs call the king the greeting, and from this comes the saying of Amr bin Ma’dikarib: I visit Abu Qaboos to pay my respects to him with my soldiers. Among them is the saying of Zuhair bin Janab al-Kalbi: Of all that the boy has received, I have received except greetings. And his saying: And their last supplication, meaning: And their last supplication is: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, meaning: And their last supplication is that they say: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, and for this reason that was lightened and not stressed, because it was intended to be a narration.
10:11: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if God were to hasten the response to people’s supplications for evil, which is when it is harmful to them in life or wealth, their hastening for good, he says: like His hastening them for good by answering them when they supplicate Him for it, their term would have been fulfilled for them, he says: they would have perished, and He would hasten death for them, which is (the term). What he meant by saying: to finish is to finish them for their sake, and to throw them away, as Abu Dhu’ayb said: And upon them are two chains of narration, which David ruled, or the making of the coats of mail was followed. So We leave those who do not expect to meet Us, meaning: We leave those who do not fear Our punishment, and do not believe in the Resurrection or the Hereafter, in their transgression, meaning: in their rebellion and insolence, wandering blindly, meaning: they hesitate. Rather, the Most High, the Praised, informed about these infidels regarding the Resurrection with what He informed about them, of their transgression and their hesitation regarding it when He hastened to answer their prayers for evil if He answered them, that this was calling them to draw closer to the idol that one of them associates with Him, or He added that to it being from his actions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if God were to hasten for the people the evil as they hasten for the good, he said: A person’s statement when he is angry about his child and his money: May God not bless him and curse him! Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if God were to hasten for the people the evil as they hasten for the good, he said: A person’s saying to his child or his wealth when he is angry with him: Bless him and curse him! If God were to hasten to respond to them in that, as He responds to the good, He would destroy them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if God were to hasten for the people the evil as they hasten for the good, he said: A person’s saying to his child and his wealth when he is angry with him: O God, do not bless him and curse him, “Their term would have been fulfilled for them,” he said: He would have destroyed the one he invoked against and caused him to die. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if God were to hasten for the people the evil as they hasten for the good, he said: What a man says to his son when he is angry with him or his money: O God, do not bless him and curse him! God said: Their term would have been fulfilled for them, he said: He would have destroyed the one who called down a curse on him and caused him to die. He said: Then leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us, he said: He says: We do not destroy the polytheists, but leave them wandering blindly in their transgression. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And if God were to hasten evil for the people as they hasten good, he said: It is a man’s supplication against himself and his wealth for something he would hate to be answered for. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Their term would have been fulfilled for them, he said: We would have destroyed them. And he recited: He did not leave on its back any creature (Fatir 35:45). He said: He would have destroyed them all. And the accusative of his saying: their hastening, is by the occurrence of (ya’ajil) upon it, like the saying of the one who says: (I stood up today as you stand up) meaning: I stood up as you stand up, and it is not a source of (ya’ajil), because if it were a source, it would not be appropriate for (kaf) - I mean the kaf of comparison - to enter into it. The readings differed regarding his saying: Their term would have been fulfilled for them. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: Their term was completed for them, in a way that does not mention the agent, with the qaf of qada in the damma and the term in the nominative case. The majority of the people of the Levant read: Their term would have been fulfilled for them, meaning: God would have fulfilled their term. Abu Jaafar said: They are two readings that agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. However, I read it as if the doer was not named, because this is what most people read.
10:12: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And when a person is afflicted with hardship and distress, he calls upon Us to his side, meaning he seeks help from Us to relieve that from him, to his side, meaning lying on his side, or sitting or standing, in the state he is in when that harm befalls him, then when We remove his harm from him, meaning when We relieve him of the distress that befell him, he goes on as if he had never called upon Us for a harm that had befallen him, meaning he continues in his original way before the harm befell him, and he forgets what he was in of hardship and affliction or pretends to forget it, and he abandons thanking his Lord who relieved him of what had befallen him of affliction when he sought refuge in Him, and he returns to polytheism and calling upon gods and idols as lords with Him. God Almighty says: Thus was made attractive to the transgressors what they were doing. He says: Just as this person whose characteristics we described was made attractive to continue in his disbelief after God removed from him the harm that was in him, so was made attractive to those who went too far in lying about God and His prophets, and went beyond what God permitted them to say about them, what they were doing of disobedience to God and associating partners with Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: He called us to his side, he said: lying down.
10:13: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We destroyed the nations who denied the messengers of God before you, O you who associate others with their Lord, when they were unjust, meaning when they associated others with God and disobeyed God’s command and prohibition, and their messengers came to them, from God, with clear proofs, which are the signs and arguments that show the truthfulness of the one who brought them. The meaning of the statement: Their messengers came to them with clear signs that they were true, and they were not to believe, meaning: these nations that We destroyed were not to believe in their messengers and believe them in what they led them to of the oneness of God and the sincerity of worship to Him, thus do We recompense the criminal people, meaning: God Almighty says: Just as We destroyed these generations before you, O polytheists, for their injustice to themselves, their denial of their messengers, and their rejection of their advice, so will I do to you and destroy you just as I destroyed them for your denial of your Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your injustice to yourselves by associating partners with your Lord. If you do not repent and turn to God from your polytheism, then among the rewards of the disbeliever in Me for his disbelief with Me is that I destroy him with My wrath in this world and cause him to enter the Fire in the Hereafter.
10:14: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Then We made you, O people, successors after these generations whom We destroyed when they committed injustice, succeeding them on the earth, and being in it after them, So that We may see how you will act, meaning: So that your Lord may see how your actions compare to the actions of those nations who were destroyed before you because of their sins and disbelief in their Lord, so that you may follow their example in this, and thus deserve the punishment they deserved, or that you may deviate from their path and believe in God and His Messenger and acknowledge the resurrection after death, and thus deserve a great reward from your Lord, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then We made you successors on the earth after them to see how you would act, he mentioned to us that Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: Our Lord has spoken the truth. He did not make us successors except to see how our deeds are. Show God the best of your deeds by night and by day, in secret and in public. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Zaid bin Awf Abu Rabia Fahd told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila: That Awf bin Malik said to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him: I saw in a dream as if a cause was lowered from the sky, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was revived. Then it was lowered and Abu Bakr was revived. Then the people gathered around the pulpit, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, was three cubits away from the pulpit. Umar said: Leave your dream, we have no interest in it! When Umar became caliph, he said: O Awf, your dream! He said: Do you have any need for my dream? Or did you not rebuke me? He said: Woe to you! I hate for you to announce the death of the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace! So he narrated the dream to him, and when he reached: (The people gathered around the pulpit by these three cubits), he said: As for the first of them, he will be the caliph. As for the second, he will not fear the blame of the blamers in God’s cause. As for the third, he will be a martyr. He said: God says: Then We made you successors on the earth after them to see how you would act. You have been made successors, O son of Umm Umar, so see how you act. As for His statement: (For I do not fear in God the blame of a blamer), then whatever God wills. As for His statement: (For I am a witness), then I am a witness for Umar, and the Muslims are surrounding him! Then he said: Indeed, God is able to do whatever He wills.
10:15: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And when the verses of the Book of God which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, are recited to these polytheists, clear proofs, clear, and indicative of the truth, those who do not expect to meet Us will say, meaning: those who do not fear Our punishment, nor are certain of the return to Us, nor believe in the resurrection, will say to you: Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it, meaning or something else. Say, to them, O Muhammad, It is not for me to change it of my own accord, meaning: from myself. The change that they asked him to do, as mentioned, was to change the verse of threat into a verse of promise, and the verse of promise into a threat, and the forbidden into permissible, and the permissible into forbidden. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform them that that is not up to him, and that that is up to the One whose judgment cannot be rejected, and whose ruling cannot be followed, but rather he is a messenger conveying the message and being commanded and followed. And His statement: I only follow what is revealed to me, meaning: Say to them: I only follow, O people, in everything I command you to do and forbid you from doing, except what my Lord sends down to me and commands me to do. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day, meaning: I fear from God, if I disobey His command, change the rulings of His Book, and alter His revelation, and disobey Him thereby, the punishment of a tremendous Day, and that is: the Day when every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people drunk, but they are not drunk.
10:16: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet, explaining the proof against these polytheists who said to him: Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it, “Say” to them, O Muhammad, If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, meaning: I would not have recited this Qur’an to you, O people, since He did not send it down to me and command me to recite it to you, nor would I have made you aware of it, meaning: I would not have informed you of it, for I have remained among you a lifetime before it, meaning: I have remained among you for forty years before I recited it to you, and before my Lord revealed it to him, Do you not understand, that if I were to claim to have said something that was not mine, I would have claimed it in my youth and youth, and before the time I recited it to you? Today, if it had not been revealed to me and I had not been commanded to recite it to you, I would have had a way out of opposing you, and ample room, in the state I was in with you before it was revealed to me and I was commanded to recite it to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: nor do I make you aware of it, nor do I inform you. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: If God had willed, He would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, meaning: If God had willed, He would not have taught it to you. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: If God had willed, He would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, meaning: He would not have warned you about it. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, ‘Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it.’ This is what the polytheists of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he said to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, ‘If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I have remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?’” He remained for forty years. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Say, ‘If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would I have made it known to you,’ nor would I have informed you of it. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to recite: And I did not inform you of it, meaning: I did not inform you of it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: nor did He make you aware of it, meaning: nor did God make you aware of it. Abu Jaafar said: This reading that was reported from Al-Hasan, from the people of Arabic, is wrong. Al-Farra’ used to say about this: It was reported that Al-Hasan said: And I did not protect you from it. He said: If there is a language for it other than darayt and adrayt, then perhaps Al-Hasan went with it. As for it being correct from darayt or adrayt, then no, because if the letter ya and waw are opened before them and are still, they are correct and do not change to an alif, like qadayt or da’wat. Perhaps Al-Hasan went with his nature and eloquence and hamzated it, because it is similar to dar’at al-hud and the like. And sometimes the Arabs make a mistake in the letter if another hamzah is similar to it, so they hamzate the one that is not hamzated. I heard a woman from Tayy saying: I mourned my husband with verses, and they say: I milked the pilgrimage and I milked the gruel, but they are mistaken, because I milked may be said to quench the thirst of a camel, and I milked refers to colostrum, the colostrum of a sheep, and I mourned my husband refers to I milked the milk, if you milked the milk with yogurt, then that is the mourning. Some of the Basrans said: There is no basis for this reading of Al-Hasan, because it is from (adrayt) like (atayt), except that the language of Banu Uqayl is (atat), meaning: I gave, the ya’ is changed to an alif, the poet said: The people of Yamamah have declared war on the famous tribe of Kanasat Al-Aghar. He wants: like a forelock, this was narrated on the authority of Al-Mufaddal, and Zaid Al-Khail said: By God, I am not afraid of becoming a vagabond. There are no Qais on earth who drive camels. He said: It remains. The poet said: I would have rebuked a heart that does not fear a rebuker, for the one who has gone astray has not heeded her call. He wants: prohibition. He said: And all of this is according to the reading of Al-Hasan, and it is not recommended. He said: And Tayyi’ makes every ya’ that is preceded by a kasra an alif. They say: (This is a jarah), and in (the collarbone) (tarqah) and (the urqowah) (iraqah). He said: And some of Tayyi’ said: (Qad laqat Fazarah), deleting the ya’ from (laqit) because he could not change it to an alif, because of the sukoon of the ta’, so two sukoon letters meet. And he said: Yunus claimed that (Nasa) and (Rida) are a well-known language. The poet said: And I was informed of the symptoms of the one with a large belly, who forgot or pretended to forget to count the loyalists. Another narration was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the recitation of this, which is: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Al-Mualla bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid bin Hanzala told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he used to recite: Say, ‘If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor warned you of it.’ Abu Ja`far said: The reading that we do not find it permissible to exclude is the reading that the regions read: Say, ‘If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would I have made it known to you,’ meaning: I would not have informed you of it, nor made you aware of it.
10:17: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these polytheists who attributed to you a lie in what you brought from your Lord: Which creation is more transgressive, and more clearly said in the wrong place, than one who fabricated a lie against God, and falsely fabricated against Him, or denied His signs, meaning: His proofs, His messengers, and the verses of His Book? God Almighty says to him: Say to them: What you have attributed me to is not more amazing than your lying about your Lord, and your fabricating against Him, and your denying His signs, Indeed, the criminals will not succeed, meaning: Those who committed disbelief in this world will not succeed on the Day of Resurrection, when they meet their Lord, nor will they attain success.
10:18: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And these polytheists, whose description I have described to you, O Muhammad, worship other than God, who does not harm them at all nor benefit them, in this world or in the Hereafter. And these are the gods and idols that they used to worship, and they say, ‘These are our intercessors’ with God, meaning: that they used to worship them hoping for their intercession with God. God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say to them, Do you inform God of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? He said: Do you inform God of what is not in the heavens or on the earth? That is because the gods do not intercede for them with God in the heavens or on the earth. And the polytheists used to claim that they interceded for them with God. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: Do you inform God that what does not intercede in the heavens or on the earth will intercede for you in them? This is false and you do not know its truth or validity. Rather, God knows that this is contrary to what you say, and that it does not intercede for anyone, nor does it benefit or harm. Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. He says: Exaltation of God and His being above what these polytheists do, of associating in His worship that which neither harms nor benefits, and their fabricating lies about Him.
10:19: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And mankind were only people of one religion and one faith, but they differed in their religion, and their paths diverged in that, And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, meaning: and had it not been for God’s predestination that He would not destroy a people except after their appointed times had expired, it would have been decided between them concerning that over which they differ, meaning: it would have been decided between them that the people of falsehood among them would be destroyed, and the people of truth would be saved. We have explained the difference of opinion among those who differed regarding the meaning of this in Surat Al-Baqarah, in His statement: Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets (al-Baqarah 2:213). We have explained the correct statement regarding this with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And mankind were but one community, then they differed, when one of the sons of Adam killed his brother. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.
10:20: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And these polytheists say: Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad from his Lord? He says: Knowledge and evidence by which we know that Muhammad is right in what he says? God said to him: Then say, O Muhammad, The unseen belongs only to God, meaning: No one knows who does that except Him, may He be glorified, because no one knows the unseen - which is the secret and hidden of matters - except God. So await, O people, God's judgment between us, by hastening His punishment for the one among us who is wrong, and revealing the truth against him, for I am with you among those who await that. So God Almighty did that, and He judged between them and Him by killing them with the sword on the day of Badr.
10:21: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And when We provide the polytheists with relief after distress, and ease after the hardship that has befallen them. It was said: It means rain after drought, and ad-Dara’ means hardship, and mercy means relief. He says: Then they have a plan against Our signs, mocking and denying, as: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: If they have a plan against Our verses, he said: mockery and denial.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And His saying: “Say: God is swifter in plotting,” God Almighty says: Say, to these polytheists who mock our arguments and proofs, O Muhammad, God is swifter in plotting, meaning: He is swifter in plotting against you, and in luring you and punishing you, from you, from plotting against the signs of God. The Arabs are satisfied with (if) from (fa`alt) and (fa`alu), so (the verb) was omitted with it. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has befallen them, they plot against Our verses, so they plot is sufficient for they plot. “Our messengers write down what you plot,” meaning: Our guardians whom We send to you, O people, write down what you plot in Our verses.
10:22: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God is the One who guides you, O people, on land on your back, and in the sea in the ark, until you are in the ark, which are the ships, and it sails with them, meaning: the ark sails with the people, with a good wind, in the sea, and they rejoice in it, meaning: the passengers of the ark rejoiced in the good wind with which they travel, and the ha in His statement: with it, refers back to the good wind. A violent wind came to it, meaning: A violent wind came to the ark, meaning a strong wind. The Arabs say: A stormy wind, and a storm, and The wind has blown, and blew, and It has blown, in Bani Asad, as mentioned. Some of Bani Dubayr said: Even if a disturbing wind blows in it, and its sound thunders, it roars And the waves came upon them from every side, God Almighty says: And the passengers of the ship were faced with waves from every side, and they thought that they were surrounded, meaning: And they thought that destruction had surrounded them and was imminent, They called upon God, sincerely devoting their religion to Him, meaning: They sincerely called upon God there, without their idols and gods, and their refuge at that time was to God, not them, as: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Call upon God, making religion sincere to Him, he said: If harm befalls them at sea, they make supplication to Him sincerely. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Umar bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, regarding his statement: devoutly for Him in religion, “Come on, come on,” its interpretation is: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has befallen them to the end of the verse, he said: These polytheists call upon God with what they call upon, so when adversity comes, they call upon none but God, and when He saves them, then at once they associate partners with Him. If You save us from this hardship we are in, we will surely be among the grateful for Your blessings and for saving us from what we are in, by our sincere worship of You and our dedication to obedience, without the deities and rivals. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: He is the One who guides you. The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: He is the One Who guides you from al-siyar with a seen. Abu Jaafar Al-Qari’ read it as: He is the One Who spreads you out from spreading, and that is spreading, from the saying of the speaker: I spread out the garment, and that is spreading it out and spreading it from folding it. Abu Jaafar directed the meaning of this to the fact that God sends His servants and spreads them out on land and sea, and it is close in meaning to the movement. He said: And they sailed with them with a good wind, and he said in other places: In the laden ship, so he made it singular, (Ya-Sin 36:41). Al-Falak is a name for the singular and the plural, and it is masculine and feminine. He said: And they ran with them, and he said: He is the one who guides you, so he addressed them, then returned to reporting on the absent. I have explained that in more than one place in the book, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The answer to his statement: Until you were in the ship, “a violent wind came upon it.” As for the answer to his statement: And they thought that they were surrounded, it is: They called upon God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely.
10:23: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: So when God saved those who thought in the sea that they were surrounded, from the hardship they were in, they broke their promise to God, and transgressed on the land, and transgressed therein to other than what God had permitted them to do, from disbelieving in Him, and committing sins against Him on its surface. God says: O people, your aggression which you transgress is only against yourselves, and it is you who wrong yourselves. And this that you are in, the enjoyment of the life of this world, meaning: That is a provision by which you will attain in your immediate worldly life. According to this interpretation, transgression is raised by the pronoun referring back to it in His statement: against yourselves, and His statement: the enjoyment of worldly life is raised in the meaning: that is the enjoyment of worldly life, just as He said: They did not remain except for an hour of a day of notification, (al-Ahqaf 46:35), meaning: this is a notification. It may be possible that the meaning of this is: Your transgression in this worldly life is only against yourselves because through your disbelief you earn the wrath of God, the enjoyment of this worldly life, as if he said: Your transgression is only the enjoyment of this worldly life, so (transgression) is raised by (enjoyment), and against yourselves is from the connection of (transgression). And the reading of (enjoyment) was raised except for Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq, who made it accusative, meaning: Your transgression against yourselves is only a provision in the life of this world, so he made (transgression) raised by his saying: against yourselves, and (enjoyment) accusative as a state. And His statement: Then to Us is your return, meaning: Then to Us after that is your return and your destination, and that is after death. Then We will inform you of what you used to do, meaning: So We will inform you on the Day of Resurrection of what you used to do in this world of disobedience to God, and We will reward you for your past deeds in this world.
10:24: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The example of what you boast about in this world and brag about of its adornments and wealth, along with the turbidity and annoyance that has been caused by that, and its disappearance by annihilation and death, is like the example of water that We have sent down from the sky, meaning: like rain that We have sent down from the sky to the earth, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it, meaning: so that with that rain various types of vegetation grew, some mixed with others, like. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The example of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it. He said: It mingled and grew with the water every color of what people eat, such as wheat, barley, and all the grains of the earth, legumes, and fruits, and what livestock and beasts eat of grass and pastures. And His saying: Until the earth takes on its adornment, meaning: its beauty and splendor appear, and is beautified, meaning: it is decorated, and its people think, meaning: the people of the earth, that they have power over it, meaning: over what it produces. The report was excluded from the earth and the meaning was for the plant, since what was meant by it was understood in the address. And His statement: Our command came to it by night or by day, meaning: it came to the earth. Our command, meaning: Our decree to destroy whatever plants were on it, either by night or by day. So We made it, meaning: We made whatever was on it, a harvest, meaning: cut off and uprooted from its roots. Rather, it is harvested and has been changed to harvested. “As if it had not sung yesterday,” he says: as if those crops and plants had not been growing and standing on the surface of the earth before that yesterday. Its origin is from: So-and-so is rich in such-and-such a place, he resides there, as Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani said: I sang about that, since they are your neighbors, with a message of affection and courtesy. He says: Thus, destruction will come upon what you boast about of your world and its adornments, and it will destroy and ruin it, just as our command and decree destroyed the vegetation of this earth after its beauty and splendor, until it became as if it had never flourished yesterday, as if there had never been any vegetation on its surface before that. God Almighty says: Thus do We explain the verses in detail for a people who give thought. He says: Just as We have explained to you, O people, the example of this world and made you aware of its rulings and its affairs, thus do We explain Our arguments and proofs to those who think, consider, and consider. He has singled out the people of thought for this, because they are the people who distinguish between matters and examine the truth of any doubts that arise in people’s hearts. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. He said that: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: Until the earth takes on its adornment, the verse, yes, by God, if he clings to the world and is greedy for it, the world will soon spit him out and finish him off. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And it was adorned, he said: it grew and became beautiful. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Harith ibn Hisham, he said: I heard Marwan reciting this verse from the pulpit: ((Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified and its people think that they have power over it. And God would not destroy it except for the sins of its people)), he said: I have recited it, but it is not in the Mushaf. So Abbas ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas said: This is how Ibn Abbas recites it. So they sent for Ibn Abbas and he said: This is how Ubayy ibn Ka`b recited it to me. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: As if you had not been rich yesterday, he says: As if you had not lived, as if you had not enjoyed. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, he said, I heard Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman say: In my father’s recitation: “As if it had never flourished yesterday, and We did not destroy it except for the sins of its people. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who give thought.” There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And it was adorned. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as wazaynatu, meaning wazaynatu, but they assimilated the ta’ into the zay, because their points of articulation are close together, and they inserted an alif to reach its reading, since the ta’ had been quiescent, and a quiescent letter is not used to begin with. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Raja’, Al-A’raj, and a group of others, that they read it as: wa azinatu and it was decorated, on the example of af’altu I did. Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading for this is: And it was adorned, because the evidence from the readings agrees on it.
10:25: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His servants: O people, do not seek the world and its adornments, for its destiny is to perish and disappear, just as the destiny of the plant that God has given as an example for it is to perish and be destroyed. Rather, seek the everlasting Hereafter, and work for it, and seek what is with God through His obedience, for God calls you to His home, which is His gardens that He has prepared for His friends, so that you may be saved from worries and sorrows in them, and be safe from the perishing of what is in them of bliss and honor that He has prepared for whoever enters them. He guides whomever He wills of His creation and grants him success in finding the straight path, which is Islam, which He, the Most High, has made a means of attaining His pleasure, and a path for whoever rides it and follows it to His gardens and honor, as: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: God is peace, and his home is Paradise. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And God invites to the home of peace,” he said: God is peace, and His home is Paradise. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, ‘It was said to me: “Let your eyes sleep, let your heart understand, and let your ears hear.” So my eyes slept, my heart understood, and my ears heard. Then it was said: “A master built a house, then made a banquet, then sent an inviter. Whoever answered the inviter entered the house, ate from the banquet, and the master was pleased with him. Whoever did not answer the inviter did not enter the house, did not eat from the banquet, and the master was not pleased with him.” So God is the master, the house is Islam, the banquet is Paradise, and the inviter is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And God invites to the home of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path,” he mentioned to us that it is written in the Torah: O seeker of good, come, and O seeker of evil, desist. Al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabsha told me, he said: Abdul Malik ibn Amr told us, he said: Ibad ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Khalid al-Asri told me, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no day in which the sun rises, except that there are two angels on either side of it calling out, and all of God’s creation hears them except the two heavy burdens: ‘O mankind, come to your Lord. Indeed, that which is little and sufficient is better than that which is much and distracts.’” He said: And this was revealed in the Qur’an in His statement: “And God invites to the home of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.” Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Layth bin Sa`d, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Jabir bin `Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and said: I saw in a dream that Gabriel was at my head and Michael was at my feet, and one of them said to the other: Give him an example! He said: Listen, your ear hears, and understand, your heart understands. Your example and that of your nation is like that of a king who took a house, then built a house in it, then held a banquet in it, then sent a messenger inviting the people to his food. Some of them responded to the messenger and some of them left him. So God is the King, the house is Islam, the house is Paradise, and you, O Muhammad, are the Messenger. Whoever responds to you enters Islam, and whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats what is in it.
10:26: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: For those of His creation who worshipped God well in this world, and obeyed Him in what He commanded and forbade, the best. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the best and the increase that He promised to the good-doers among His creation. Some of them said: Al-Husna is Paradise, which God has made a reward for the good-doers among His creation, and the addition to it is looking at God. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amer bin Saad, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking at the face of their Lord. Sufyan told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amer bin Saad, on the authority of Saeed bin Nimran, on the authority of Abu Bakr: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking at the face of God. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amer ibn Saad, For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking at the face of their Lord. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of `Amir ibn Sa`d, he said regarding this verse: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: The more is looking at the face of the Most Merciful. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Muslim ibn Nadhir, on the authority of Hudhayfah: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking upon the face of their Lord. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Sharik told us, he said, I heard Abu Ishaq say about the statement of God: And more, he said: Looking at the face of the Most Merciful. Ali bin Isa told me, Shababah told us, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, I heard Abu Tamima al-Hujaimi narrating on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will send a crier to the people of Paradise calling out: Has God fulfilled for you what He promised you? They will look at what God has prepared for them of honor and will say: Yes! He will say: For those who have done good is the best and more, looking at the face of the Most Merciful. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, who said, Abu Tamima Al-Hujaimi told us, who said, I heard Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari delivering a sermon from the pulpit of Basra, saying: God will send an angel to the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection and say: O people of Paradise, has God fulfilled for you what He promised you? They will look and see ornaments, garments, fruits, rivers, and pure spouses. They will say: Yes, God has fulfilled for us what He promised us! Then the angel will say: Has God fulfilled for you what He promised you? three times. They will not miss anything of what they were promised. They will say: Yes! He will say: "Something remains for you. God says: 'For those who do good is the best and more.' Beware, the best is Paradise, and the more is looking at the face of God." Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Shabib told me, on the authority of Abaan, on the authority of Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi: that he heard Abu Musa al-Ash’ari narrating on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “On the Day of Resurrection, God will send a caller who will call out to the people of Paradise in a voice that the first and the last of them will hear: ‘God has promised you the best and more. The best is Paradise, and the more is looking at the face of the Most Merciful.’” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking at the face of their Lord. And he recited: And neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces, he said: after looking at the face of their Lord.
