Al-Muntha told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Al-Mughira, he said, Thabit told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, regarding His statement: And more, he said: It was said to him: What do you think of His statement: For those who do good is the best and more? He said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and are given therein what they were given of honor and bliss, he said: It will be called out: O people of Paradise, God has promised you more,” and He will reveal Himself to them. Ibn Abi Laila said: What do you think of them when their scales become heavy, and when the scrolls are in their right hands, and when they cross the bridge of Hell and enter Paradise, and are given therein what they were given of honor and bliss? All of that was nothing in what they saw!... He said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, and Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking upon the face of their Lord.... He said, Al-Hajjaj and Mu'alla bin Asad told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, who said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, He will say to them: There remains something of your right that you have not been given! He said: Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, will appear to them. He said: Then everything they have given will seem small to them. He said: Then He said: For those who have done good is the best and more, He said: The best is Paradise, and the more is looking upon the face of their Lord, and no darkness or humiliation will cover their faces after that. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila: For those who do good is the best and more, meaning looking at the face of God. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God: For those who do good is the best and more, looking at the Lord. Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated that Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, regarding this verse: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, it will be called out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God! They will say: What is it? Did You not make our faces white, make our scales heavy, admit us into Paradise, and save us from Hell? Then the veil will be lifted and He will appear to them. By God, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him. The wording of the hadith is that of Amr. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Suhaib, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘For those who do good is the best and more. ’ He said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, a caller will call out: ‘O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God that He wants to fulfill for you. ’ They will say: ‘What is it? Has God not made our scales heavy and made our faces white? ’” Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith, such as the hadith of Amr bin Ali and Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman.... He said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Namran, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: looking at the face of God, the Blessed and Most High.... He said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amer bin Saad, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement: For those who do good is the best and more, it has reached us that when the believers entered Paradise, a caller called out to them: God has promised you the best, which is Paradise, and as for the more, it is looking at the face of the Most Merciful. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka’b bin Ujrah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘For those who do good is the best and more,’ he said: The more is looking upon the face of the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted be He.”... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: Al-Hasna means freshness, and al-Zidah means looking at the face of God. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, he said, I heard Zuhair, on the authority of someone who heard Abu al-Aaliyah, he said, “Abi ibn Ka’b told us: that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God: ‘For those who do good is the best and more,’ he said: The best is Paradise, and the more is looking at the face of God.” Others said in Al-Ziyadah: Yahya bin Talha told us, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: For those who do good is the best and more. He said: The more is a room made of a single pearl with four doors. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, something similar, except that he said: It has four doors.... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, like the hadith of Yahya bin Talha, on the authority of Fadil, exactly the same. Others said: Al-Hasna is one of the good deeds for one, and Al-Ziyada is the doubling to complete ten. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: For those who do good is the best and even more, he said: It is like his statement: And with Us is more, (Qaf: 35), meaning: He will reward them for their deeds and increase them from His bounty. And He said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, but whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged, (Al-An`am: 160). Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Alqamah bin Qais: For those who do good is the best and even more. I said: This is the best, but what is the even more? He said: Did you not see that God says: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof? (Al-An`am: 160). Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan used to say about this verse: For those who do good is the best and more, he said: The increase in the good deed is ten times its value up to seven hundred times. Others said: Al-Husna is a good deed like Hasanah, and Al-Ziyadah is an increase in forgiveness from God and His pleasure. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: For those who do good is the best, the same as it is good, and more, forgiveness and approval. Others said: The increase is what they were given in this world. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, For those who do good is the best and more, he said: The best is Paradise, and and more is what He gave them in this world, for which He will not hold them accountable on the Day of Resurrection. And they read: And We gave him his reward in this world (al-Ankabut 29:27). He said: Whatever He gave him of what he loved in this world, He hastened his reward for him in it. Ibn Abbas used to say about his statement: For those who do good is the best, as follows: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: For those who do good is the best, meaning: for those who testify that there is no god but God. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard is that God, the Blessed and Exalted, promised the righteous among His servants for their good deeds the best, that He would reward them for their obedience to Him with Paradise, and that He would make their faces white, and He promised them with the best and more. And among the additions to their admission to Paradise is that He would honor them by looking at Him, and that He would give them rooms of pearls, and that He would increase their forgiveness and pleasure. All of that is from the additions of God’s giving to them in addition to the best that God has made for the people of His Paradise. And our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, included in His saying: and more, the additions to the best, and He did not specify one of them over the other. It is not strange that God’s grace should gather that for them, rather all of that will be gathered for them, God willing. So the most correct of the sayings in this regard is that it should be general, as He, may He be glorified and exalted, has made it general. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.” Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And neither darkness nor humiliation shall cover their faces, is that neither gloom nor eclipse shall cover their faces, until they become as if darkness had covered them from grief. And Qatar means dust, and it is the plural of Qatrah, and from it the poet said: Crowned with the king's robe, followed by waves above which you can see the banners and the qitra It means dust. And no humiliation, nor disgrace. Those are the companions of Paradise, meaning: those whose description has been described are the people of Paradise and its inhabitants, and whoever is in it, they are therein eternally, meaning: they are therein abiding forever, it will not perish, so they will fear the loss of their bliss, nor will they be expelled, so their pleasure will be spoiled for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Ibn Abi Laila used to say about his statement: And their faces will not be covered with darkness, what: Muhammad bin Mansur al-Tusi told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila: And neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces, he said: after they look at their Lord. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj and Mu’alla bin Asad told us, they said: Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And their faces shall not be covered with darkness, he said: The blackness of the faces.
10:27: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And those who committed evil deeds in this world, disobeyed God therein, and disbelieved in Him and His Messenger, the recompense for an evil deed for the evil deed he committed in this world, is like it for God’s punishment in the Hereafter, and humiliation will overwhelm them meaning: and humiliation and disgrace will cover them, because of God’s punishment of them, they will have no protector from God meaning: they will have no protector from God to prevent them, if He punishes them, to stand between Him and them. And similar to what we said about His statement: And humiliation will overwhelm them, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And humiliation will overwhelm them, he said: humiliation and hardship will overwhelm them. The Arabs differed about the meaning of araf in al-jaza’. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It was raised by the omission of for them, as if it was said: And for them is the recompense of the evil with the like of it, as he said: So fasting three days during the Hajj, (al-Baqarah 2:196), and the meaning is: So he must fast three days. He said: And if you wish, you can raise the recompense with the preposition for in his saying: The recompense of the evil with the like of it. Some Basra grammarians said: The reward is raised as a subject, and its predicate is with its like. He said: The meaning of the statement is: the reward for an evil deed is like it, and the ba was added, just as it was added in their saying: It is enough for you to say evil. Some of them denied this statement, saying: It is possible that the letter ba in hasab is redundant, because the interpretation is: If you say bad then it is sufficient for you. Since it is not included in the predicate, it is included in hasab, bi-hasabka an qiyam: If you stand then it is sufficient for you. If what comes after hasab is praised, the letter ba is included in what comes after it, like your saying: Hasabka bi-Zayd, and it is not permissible to say bi-hasabka Zayd, because Zayd is the one being praised, so it is not an interpretation of the predicate. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that al-jaza` is raised with an implied subject, meaning: For them is the recompense of an evil deed like it, because God said in the verse before it: For those who do good is the best and more, so He described what He has prepared for His friends, then followed that with the report of what God has prepared for His enemies, so it is more like the statement to say: For those who have earned evil deeds is the recompense of an evil, and if that is directed to this meaning, then the ba’ is a connection to the recompense. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “As if their faces had been covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.” Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: As if the faces of those who have committed evil deeds were covered with pieces of the night, which is the plural of piece. Qatada used to say in his interpretation of this: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: As if their faces were covered with pieces of dark night, he said: darkness of the night. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Certainly. The general reading of the regions is: Qata’an, with the opening of the ta, meaning the plural of Qata’a, and meaning that the interpretation of that is: as if a piece of the blackness of the night had covered the face of every person among them. Then that was collected and it was said: as if their faces were covered in pieces, from blackness, since it was the plural of the face. Some of the later reciters read it as qat’a with a silent ta’, meaning: as if their faces were covered with blackness from the night, and the remainder of the night, an hour of it, as He said: So set out with your family during a part of the night, (Hud 11:81 - al-Hijr 15:65), meaning: during a remainder that remained of it. He also argues that in the books of Abu: And their faces were covered by pieces of the dark night. Abu Ja`far said: The reading that I believe it is not permissible to differ from is the reading of the one who reads it with the opening of the ta’, due to the consensus of the authority among the readers of the regions on its correctness, and the anomaly of what is other than it. The other is sufficient evidence of its corruption, as its reader has departed from the reading of the people of the regions of Islam. If someone were to say to us: If what you said is correct in reading this, then what is the reason for making al-Mudhlim masculine and singular, when it is an adjective for al-Qata’, and al-Qata’ is the plural of feminine? It was said: There are two aspects to reminding of that: One of them: that it is definitely from (night), and that it is from the description of (night), so since it is indefinite, and (night) is definite, it is in the accusative case for the cut, so the meaning of the speech then is: as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night, then the alif and lam were deleted from (dark), so since it became indefinite and it is from the description of (night), it is in the accusative case for the cut. The people of Basra call what is like this a state, and the people of Kufa call it a certainty. The other side: as the poet said: If the praise of a living being spreads out to anyone The first face is the better of the two faces. And His saying: Those are the companions of the Fire, meaning: These are those whose description I have described to you, the people of the Fire who are its people. They will abide therein eternally, meaning: They will remain therein.
10:28: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And on the Day when We shall gather all creation for the place of reckoning, then We shall say at that time to those who associated with God gods and rivals, Stay where you are, meaning: Stay where you are, you polytheists, and your partners whom you used to worship besides God from the gods and idols, Then We shall separate between them, meaning: We shall separate between the polytheists and what they associated with Him. From their saying: I removed something, meaning I separated it from something else and made it separate from it. He said: We removed it, meaning to increase the action and repeat it, and he did not say: We removed it among them. It was mentioned that some of them used to read it: (Fazayilna bainha) as it was said: And do not turn your cheek away (Luqman 31:18). The Arabs do this a lot in (fa`alt), sometimes adding an alif in place of the shaddah, so they say (fa`alt) if the action is for one person. But if it is for two, they hardly say anything except (fa`alt). And their partners said, ‘You did not worship us.’ This was when those who followed disavowed those who followed them and saw the punishment and their connections were cut off, when it was said to the polytheists: Follow what you used to worship besides God, and their gods were set up for them. They said: We used to worship these! So the gods said to them: You did not worship us, as: Narrated to us on the authority of Muslim bin Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: There will be a time of great severity on the Day of Resurrection, when the gods they used to worship will be set up for them, and it will be said: These are the ones you used to worship instead of God! The gods will say: By God, we did not hear, see, or understand, and we did not know that you used to worship us! They will say: By God, we used to worship you! The gods will say to them: Sufficient is God as a witness between us and you, if we were unaware of your worship. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And the Day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated, ‘Stay where you were, you and your associates.’ So We shall separate them, he said, We shall separate them, And their associates will say, ‘It was not us that you used to worship.’ They will say, Yes, we used to worship you. They will say, “Sufficient is God as a Witness between us and you. Indeed, we were unaware of your worship.” We did not hear, see, or speak. So God said, There every soul will be made to taste what it put forth, the verse. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he interpreted al-Hashr in this context as death. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: I heard them mention on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And the Day We shall gather them all together, he said: The gathering means death. Abu Ja`far said: What we have said about this is more deserving of its interpretation, because God Almighty mentioned that He will say on that day to those who associate partners with God what He mentioned that He will say to them, and it is known that this will not happen in the grave, and that it is only report about what will be said to them and what they will say in the gathering after the resurrection.
10:29: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what the polytheists’ partners of gods and idols will say to them on the Day of Resurrection, when the polytheists will say to them: We used to worship you, God is sufficient as a witness between us and you, meaning that it will say: God is sufficient for us as a witness between us and you, O polytheists, for He knows that we do not know what you are saying, Indeed, we were unaware of your worship, meaning: We were only unaware of your worship of us instead of God, not perceiving it nor knowing it, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, we were unaware of your worship, he said: Everything that is worshipped other than God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Warqa`, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said: Indeed, we were unaware of your worship, he said: Everything that was worshipped other than God says that.
10:30: Abu Ja`far said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: There every soul will be tested, [so some of them read it] with the letter ba’, meaning: at that time every soul will be tested for what good or evil it has done. Among those who read and interpreted it in this way was Mujahid. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Warqa`, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: There every soul will be tested for what it put forth, he said: it will be tested. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. A group of people from Kufa and some people from Hijaz read it as: Every soul will recite what it has put forth, with a ta’. Readers of this also differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: Its meaning and interpretation is: There, every soul will be followed for what it did in this world on that Day. A similar report was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from a source and chain of transmission other than Murtadha, that he said: Every people will be represented on the Day of Resurrection by what they used to worship besides God, and they will follow them until they are led to the Fire. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: There every soul will be made to account for what it put forth. Some of them said: Rather, its meaning is: He recites the book of his good deeds and bad deeds, meaning he reads, as God Almighty said: And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out (al-Isra’ 17:13). Others said: recite means see. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: (There every soul will be recounted what it put forth), he said: what it did, (will be recounted) it will see it. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which was recited by the imams of the recitations, and they are close in meaning. That is because whoever follows up in the Hereafter what he did in the worldly life, he will be attacked by it at its source, and there he will be informed of what he did in the worldly life of good or bad. And whoever reports what he did in the worldly life of his deeds in the Hereafter, he will only be informed after his destination to where he was placed by what he did in the worldly life of his deeds. So in both cases he is following up on what he did in the worldly life of his deeds, and he will be tested. So whichever of them the reciter recites, as we have described, he is correct in that. As for his statement: And they will be returned to God, their true Master, he is saying: And these polytheists will return on that day to God, who is their Lord and their Master, the Truth, without doubt, without what they claimed that they had as masters of gods and rivals. And what they used to invent will be lost to them, he says: And what they used to invent of slander and lies against God will be nullified from them, by their claiming that their idols are partners to God, and that they bring them closer to Him, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to invent will be lost to them, he said: What they used to call upon with Him of rivals and gods, what they used to invent of gods, and that is because they made them rivals and gods with God, a fabrication and a lie.
10:31: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate idols with God, Who provides for you from the sky, the rain and the drops, and causes its sun to rise for you, and covers its night, and brings forth its brightness, and from the earth, your sustenance and nourishment that it produces for you, and the fruits of its trees, Who has control over the hearing and the sight, meaning: Or who is it that has control over your hearing and your sight with which you hear: that He increases their strength or takes them away from you, making you deaf, and your sight with which you see: that He illuminates them for you and gives them light, or takes away their light, making you blind and unable to see, And who brings forth the living from the dead, meaning: And who brings forth the living thing from the dead, And brings forth the dead from the living, meaning: And brings forth the dead thing from the living. We have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation, and the correct statement in our view regarding that, with the evidence indicating its correctness, in Surat Al Imran, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And who manages the affair? And say to them: Who manages the affair of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and your affair and the affair of creation? “They will say: God.” He, the Most High, says: They will answer you by saying: The One who does all of that is God. “Then say: Do you not fear God?” He says: Do you not fear God’s punishment for your polytheism and your claiming a Lord other than this description, and your worshipping with Him someone who does not provide for you anything, nor does he possess for you any harm or benefit, nor does he do any action?
10:32: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His creation: O people, this is the one who does these actions, provides for you from the sky and the earth, owns hearing and sight, brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and manages the matter, God is your Lord, the Truth, there is no doubt about that, So what is there after the Truth except misguidance? He says: What is there other than the Truth except misguidance, which is deviation from the right path? He says: If the Truth is this, then your claiming someone other than Him as a god and Lord is misguidance and deviation from the Truth, there is no doubt about that, So how are you turned away? He says: So which direction do you turn away from guidance and the Truth, and do you follow other than them, while you acknowledge that what you are turning away from is the Truth?
10:33: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Just as these polytheists were turned away from the truth to misguidance, Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect, meaning: His judgment and decree were incumbent upon them in the past from His knowledge, upon those who disobeyed, so they departed from the obedience of their Lord to His disobedience and disbelieved in Him, that they do not believe, meaning: they do not believe in the Oneness of God or in the prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:34: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, Is there among your partners, meaning among the gods and idols, one who initiates creation and then repeats it, meaning: who creates something from nothing, so He creates it from the beginning, then repeats it, meaning: then He annihilates it after creating it, then He restores it to its form before He annihilated it, for they are not able to claim that for them. And in that is the conclusive proof and clear evidence that in their claim that they are lords, and they are partners to God in worship, they are liars and slanderers. So say to them then, O Muhammad: God initiates creation and creates it from nothing, and brings it into being from nothing, then He annihilates it if He wills, then He restores it if He wills to its form before annihilation, How then are you deluded, meaning: So in what direction do you turn away from the intended path and the path of guidance and guidance? - Like: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan: How are you being turned away? He said: How are you being turned away? We have explained the differences of opinion among those who differ in their interpretation of His statement: How are you deluded? The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is based on evidence in Surat Al-An’am.
10:35: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists, Is there among your partners, those whom you call upon besides God, and that is their gods and idols, anyone who guides to the truth, meaning: who guides a lost person from his misguidance to the right path, and directs a deviant from guidance to the clear straight path? For they are not able to claim that their gods and idols guide a lost person or direct a deviant person. This is because if they claimed that of them, then observation would belie them, and its inability to do so would be demonstrated by testing with observation. If they say: No, and acknowledge that, then say to him: God guides the one who has gone astray from guidance to the truth. Is he who guides, O people, one who has gone astray to the truth, and deviated from the right path to the right path, more worthy of being followed, to what he calls to, or he who does not guide unless he is guided? There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina read it as: Amman la yahdi who does not guide, with the ha’ pronounced as a sukoon and the dal pronounced as a shaddah. They combined two sukoon letters, and it seems that what prompted them to do that was that they had directed the root of the word to be: Amman la yahtadi who does not guide, and they found it in the script of the Qur’an in a different way than what they read, and that the ta’ was deleted because it was assimilated into the dal, so they kept the ha’ pronounced as a sukoon on its original form, and they stressed the dal in order to assimilate the ta’ into it, so the ha’ and the dal were both sukoon. They did the same in His statement: And We said to them, ‘Do not transgress on the Sabbath’ (An-Nisa’: 154), and in His statement: They will argue (Ya-Sin 36:49). Some of the readers of Mecca, Syria and Basra read it as yahidi with the opening of the ha’ and the emphasis on the dal, and they followed what the people of Medina followed in the word, except that they transferred the vowel of the ta’ from yahidi to the silent ha’, so they moved it with its vowel, and they assimilated the ta’ into the dal and stressed it. Some of the Kufan reciters read it as: (yahdi), with the opening of the ya’, the kasra of the ha’, and the shaddah of the dal, in the same way that the reciters of the people of Medina intended, except that he broke the ha’ because of the kasra of the dal in (yahtadi), because the fatha followed by a kasra in one letter was too heavy. And after that, most of the Kufians recited: Am man la yahdi or am man la yahdi with a sukoon on the ha’ and a light dal. They said: The Arabs say: hadayt meaning ahtadayt I was guided. They said: So the meaning of his saying: Am man la yahdi is: Am man la yahtidd: unless he is guided. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct reading of this is the reading of the one who reads: Am man la yahdi with the ha’ open and the dal doubled, because of what we have described as the reason for the one who reads it in this way, and that its correctness is not negated by someone with knowledge of the speech of the Arabs, and among them are those who deny it other than it. And the speech is most deserving of being read in the most eloquent of the languages in which it was revealed, the speech of God. So the interpretation of the statement is: Is he who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or he who is not guided to anything unless he is guided? Some interpreters claimed that the meaning of this is: Or someone who is not able to move from his place unless he is moved. Mujahid used to say in his interpretation of this: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not guide unless he is guided? He said: The idols. God guides from them and other than them whomever He wills to whatever He wills. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Or is he who does not guide unless he is guided? He said, he said: The idol. And His saying: What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Do you not know that the one who guides to the truth is more deserving of being followed than the one who is not guided to anything, unless someone else guides him to it? So you abandon following and worshipping the one who is not guided to anything, and follow the one who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea, and devote worship to Him alone, singling Him out for it, without associating any of your gods and idols with Him?
10:36: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And most of these polytheists follow nothing but conjecture, meaning: except what they have no knowledge of its truth and correctness, rather they are in doubt and suspicion about it, Indeed, conjecture is of no avail against the truth, meaning: Doubt is of no avail against certainty, and does not take its place in anything, nor is it of benefit when certainty is needed, Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do, God Almighty says: God is All-Knowing of what these polytheists do, of following conjecture and denying the certain truth, and He is watching them, as their conjecture is of no avail against God.
10:37: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: This Qur'an should not be invented by anyone other than God. He says: It should not be invented by anyone other than God. This is similar to His statement: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war (Al Imran 3:161), meaning: It is not for a prophet to be taken spoils of war by his companions. This is report from God, the Most High, that this Qur’an is from Him, and that He sent it down to His servant Muhammad, and a refutation from Him of the polytheists who said: It is poetry and divination, and who said: Muhammad only learns it from Yahnes the Roman. He, the Most High, says to them: This Qur’an could not have been invented by anyone other than God, because no one among creation is capable of doing that. But it is a confirmation of what was before it, God Almighty says: But it is from God. He sent it down confirming what was before it, meaning: what came before it of the books that were sent down to God’s prophets, such as the Torah, the Gospel, and other books of God that He sent down to His prophets. And a detailed explanation of the Book, meaning: And a clarification of the Book that God wrote for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and His obligations that He imposed upon them in the past from His knowledge. There is no doubt about it, meaning: There is no doubt about it that it is a confirmation of what was before it of the Book and a detailed explanation of the Book, from the Lord of the Worlds, not a fabrication from anyone other than Him nor an invention.
10:38: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists say: Muhammad invented this Qur’an from himself, so he fabricated it and made it up? Say, O Muhammad, to them: If it is as you say, that I invented it and made it up, then you are like me among the Arabs, and my tongue is like your tongue, and my speech is like your speech, so bring a surah like this Qur’an. The letter ha in his saying like it is a metaphor for the Qur’an. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The meaning of this is: Say, Bring a surah like his surah. Then surah was dropped, and the example was added to what was added to the surah, just as it was said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), meaning: And ask the people of the town. Some of them denied this statement of his, and claimed that its meaning was: Then bring a Qur’an like this Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that the surah is a surah from the Qur’an, and it is the Qur’an, even if it is not the entire Qur’an. So it was said to them: Then bring a surah like it, and it was not said: like it, because the metaphor was conveyed according to the meaning - I mean the meaning of the surah - not according to its wording, because if it had been conveyed according to its wording, it would have been said: Then bring a surah like it. “And call upon whomever you can besides God,” meaning: And call upon, O polytheists, whomever you are able to call upon from among your allies and partners to produce a surah like it, besides God, meaning: from other than God. So agree upon that and strive hard, for you will never be able to produce a surah like it. And His saying: If you are truthful, means: If you are truthful that Muhammad invented it, then bring a surah like it from all those who will help you to produce it. If you do not do that, then there is no doubt that you are lying in your claim that Muhammad invented it, because Muhammad would be nothing more than a human being like you. So if all of creation are unable to produce a surah like it, then one of them is even more unable to produce all of it.
10:39: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: What is wrong with these polytheists, O Muhammad, is that they deny you, but they deny what they do not comprehend the knowledge of, which God has revealed to you in this Qur'an, of their threat for their disbelief in their Lord, and its interpretation has not yet come to them, meaning: and after explaining what that threat that God threatened them with in this Qur'an will lead to, thus did those before them deny, God Almighty says: Just as these polytheists, O Muhammad, denied God's threat, so did the nations that came before them deny God's threat to them for their denial of their messengers and their disbelief in their Lord, Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So see, O Muhammad, how was the end of the disbelief of those who disbelieved in God. Did We not destroy some of them with the earthquake, some of them with the sinking, and some of them with the drowning? He says: The end of those who deny you and reject My signs from among your disbelievers is like the end of those before them from among the disbelievers of the nations, if they do not repent from their disbelief and hasten to repent.
10:40: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And among your people, O Muhammad, from Quraysh, is there anyone who will believe in it, meaning: those who will believe in the Qur'an and acknowledge that it is from God, And among them is he who will not believe in it ever, meaning: and among them is he who will not believe in it and will never acknowledge it, And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters, meaning: God is most knowing of those among them who deny it, who will never believe in it, of everyone, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is behind His punishment. As for those among them whom I have decreed to believe in it, then I will accept their repentance.
10:41: Abu Ja'far said: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace: If these polytheists, O Muhammad, belie you and reject what you have brought them from your Lord, then say to them: O people, to me is my religion and my deeds, and to you is your religion and your deeds. Your deeds will not harm me, nor will my deeds harm you. Rather, every worker will be rewarded according to his deeds. You are innocent of what I do, you will not be held accountable for his crime, and I am innocent of what you do, I will not be held accountable for your crime. This is as the Almighty said: Say, ‘O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor will you worship what I worship.’ (al-Kafirun 109:1-3). It was said: This verse was abrogated, abrogated by jihad and the command to fight. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And if they deny you, then say, ‘For me is my work, and for you is your work,’ the verse, he said: He ordered him to do this, then abrogated it and ordered him to fight them.
10:42: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And among these polytheists are those who listen to your saying, Can you make the deaf hear, even if they do not understand? He says: Can you create hearing for them, even if they do not have hearing by which they understand, or am I? This is only an announcement from God to His servants that success in believing in Him is in His hand, not in anyone else’s. He says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Just as you cannot hear, O Muhammad, one from whom I have deprived hearing, so too you cannot understand My commands and prohibitions from a heart from which I have deprived the understanding of that, because I have sealed it so that it does not believe.
10:43: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And among these polytheists, the polytheists of your people, there are those who look to you, O Muhammad, and see your signs and proofs of your prophethood, but God has taken away success from them so they are not guided, and you are not able to guide them, just as you are not able to give sight to the blind by which they can be guided, Can you guide the blind even if they do not see? He says: So, O Muhammad, can you give these people who look to you and your proofs and proofs, but they are not granted sight to believe in you, even if they were blind, by which they can be guided and see? Just as you are not able to do that, nor is anyone else able to do it, and no one else is able to do it, so too you are not able to show them the path of guidance, you or anyone else, because that is in my hand and to me. This is from God Almighty, as a consolation to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a group of his people who disbelieved in him and turned away from him and denied him, and as a consolation for him for them, and an order to remove his hope of their repentance to faith in God.
10:44: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God does not do to His creation what they do not deserve from Him. He does not punish them except for their disobedience to Him, and He does not torment them except for their disbelief in Him. But the people, meaning: But the people are the ones who wrong themselves, by committing what causes them to incur God’s wrath and anger. Rather, this is an announcement from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those who believe in him, that He did not strip those about whom He, may His praise be glorified, informed us that they would not believe from the beginning, of their faith without any previous crime on their part, and an announcement that He only stripped them of it because they deserved it to be stripped away, due to sins they had committed, so the word of their Lord came true upon them, and a seal was placed on their hearts.
10:45: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And on the Day when We will gather these polytheists and assemble them in the place of reckoning, it will be as if they had only remained for an hour of a day, recognizing one another, then recognition was cut off and that hour passed. God says: Those who denied the meeting with God have certainly lost, and they were not guided. Those who denied God’s reward and punishment have been deprived of their share of goodness and have perished. And they were not guided. He says: And they were not successful in attaining the right path because of what they did in denying the meeting with God, because that earned them what they could not bear of God’s punishment.
10:46: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime some of the punishment that We promise these polytheists of your people, or We cause you to die, before We show you that in them, then to Us is their return, meaning: Their fate in every case is to Us, and their turning back, then God is Witness over what they do, meaning: God Almighty says: Then I am a witness over their actions that they used to do in this world, and I am All-Knowing of them, nothing of them is hidden from Me, and I will reward them for them when they return to Me and return, the reward they deserve, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if We show you some of what We promise them, of the torment during your lifetime, or We take you in death, before, then to Us is their return. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Warqa`, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
10:47: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And for every nation that came before you, O people, there is a messenger whom I sent to them, just as I sent Muhammad to you, calling those whom I sent to them to the religion of God and His obedience, So when their messenger comes, meaning: in the Hereafter, just as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: “And for every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes,” he said: On the Day of Resurrection. And His statement: It will be judged between them with justice, meaning: It will be judged between them with fairness, and they will not be wronged, in the recompense for their deeds at all, but the doer of good will be rewarded for his goodness. And the wrongdoer among the people of faith, God will either punish him or forgive him. And the disbeliever, he will remain in the Fire forever. So that is God’s judgment between them with justice, and that is undoubtedly justice, not injustice. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: It was judged between them with justice, he said: with fairness.
10:48: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And these polytheists from your people say, O Muhammad, When will this promise come to us, which you promise us will come to us from God, and that is the establishment of the Hour, if you are truthful, you and those who follow you, in what you promise us of that.
10:49: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those who hasten you to fulfill God’s threat, who say to you: When will the promise you are making us come to us if you are truthful? I have no control over myself, O people, meaning: I have no power to harm or benefit myself in this world or in religion, except what God wills, that is, that I have control over it, so I bring it to myself with His permission. God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: Since I am not able to do that except with His permission, then I am unable and incapable of attaining knowledge of the unseen and knowing the coming of the Hour, except with His will and permission for me to do so. For every nation there is a term, meaning: for every people there is a time for the expiration of their term and their appointed time. So when the time for the expiration of their term and the end of their lives comes, they will not delay, from it, an hour, so they are given respite and postponed, nor will they advance, before that, because God has decreed that it will not advance before the time that He has decreed and ordained.
10:50: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from your al-Nas 114:Have you considered if the punishment of God comes to you at night, meaning: at night and during the day, and the Hour comes and the Day of Judgment occurs, would you be able to repel that from yourselves? God Almighty says: What makes the punishment hasten to come down, the criminals who disbelieved in God, and they are the ones who are the only ones who will be immersed in His sea, and then they will not be able to repel it from themselves?
10:51: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: When the punishment of God befalls you, O polytheists, will you believe in it? He says: You believed in it in a state in which belief would not benefit you, and it was said to you at that time: Now you believe in it, while before now you were hastening it and denying its descent? So taste now what you used to deny. The meaning of his saying: then in this place: there, and this then here is not the one that comes with the meaning of conjunction.
10:52: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Then it will be said to those who did wrong, meaning themselves, by their disbelief in God, Taste the punishment of eternity, meaning they will taste God’s punishment that is eternal for you forever, which will never end or disappear. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn? He says: It will be said to them: So look, are you being recompensed, meaning: are you being rewarded, except for what you used to earn? He says: except for what you used to do in your life before your death of disobedience to God?
10:53: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: These polytheists from your people ask you, O Muhammad, and they say to you: Is what you say true, and what you promise us of God's punishment in the Hereafter as a recompense for what we used to commit of disobedience to God in this world? Say to them, O Muhammad: Yes, by my Lord, it is the truth, there is no doubt about it, and you cannot escape God if He wants that for you, by fleeing or refusing, rather you are in His grip, authority and kingdom, if He wants to do that to you, so fear God in yourselves.
10:54: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if every soul that disbelieved in God, and (wronged) - in this place, worshipped other than the One Who deserves to be worshipped and abandoned the obedience of the One Whom it is obligated to obey, had everything on earth, whether little or much, it would ransom itself with it, meaning it would ransom itself with all of that from the punishment of God when it witnessed it. And His statement: And they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment, meaning: And the leaders of these polytheists concealed their regret from their lowly and base ones, when they saw that the punishment of God had encompassed them, and they were certain that it would befall them, and it will be judged between them with justice, meaning: And God judged on that day between the followers and the leaders among them with justice, and they will not be wronged, meaning that He does not punish any of them except for his crime, and He does not take him for the sin of anyone, and He does not punish anyone except for those who were excused to Him in this world and warned and supported with arguments.
10:55: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Verily, everything in the heavens and everything on the earth belongs to God, and no one else has anything in it. He says: On that Day, this disbeliever will have nothing that he owns to ransom himself with from the punishment of his Lord, but all things belong to the One to Whom belongs His punishment. If he had the things that are on the earth, and ransomed himself with them, they would not be accepted from him in exchange for his punishment, and the punishment would be averted from him with them. So how is it that he has nothing to ransom himself with from it, and the punishment of God has come true upon him? God Almighty says: Verily, the promise of God is true, meaning that His punishment that He threatened these polytheists with for their disbelief is true, so they do not have to rush it, for it will undoubtedly happen to them. But most of them do not know, He says: But most of these polytheists do not know the truth of that happening to them, so they are deniers because of their ignorance of it.
10:56: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God is the Giver of life and death. It is not difficult for Him to do what He wanted to do of reviving these polytheists if He wanted to revive them after their death, nor to kill them if He wanted that. They will return to Him after their death, and they will witness what they denied of God’s threat and punishment.
10:57: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His creation: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord, meaning: a reminder that reminds you of God's punishment and frightens you with His threat, from your Lord, meaning: from your Lord. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not invent it, nor did anyone fabricate it, so that you would say: We are not certain that it is not true. Rather, He, may His praise be glorified, means by that the Qur'an, which is the instruction from God. And His statement: And a cure for what is in the breasts, meaning: And a medicine for what is in the breasts of ignorance, with which God cures the ignorance of the ignorant, so He cures their illness, and guides with it whoever He wills to guide from His creation, And guidance, meaning: It is a clarification of what is lawful and unlawful from God, and evidence of His obedience and disobedience, And mercy, with which He has mercy on whomever He wills from His creation, so He saves him from misguidance to guidance, and rescues him from destruction and ruin. And God, the Blessed and Exalted, made it a mercy for those who believe in Him, not for those who disbelieve in Him, because whoever disbelieves in Him is blind to it, and in the Hereafter his reward for disbelief in Him is eternity in the Blaze.
10:58: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who deny you and what was revealed to you from your Lord, By the grace of God, O people, with which He favored you, which is Islam, so He made it clear to you and called you to it, and by His mercy, with which He had mercy on you, so He sent it down to you, so He taught you what you did not know of His Book, and made you aware of the landmarks of your religion, which is the Qur’an, “So in that let them rejoice. It is better than what they accumulate,” meaning: The Islam to which He called them, and the Qur’an that He sent down to them, are better than what they accumulate of the debris of this world, its money and its treasures. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Azdi told me, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, regarding his statement: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice,’ he said: In the bounty of God, the Qur’an, and in His mercy, that He made you among His people. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice.’ He said: In Islam, which guided you, and in the Qur’an, which taught you. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf: Say, ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’ he said: By Islam and the Qur’an, “So in that let them rejoice. It is better than what they accumulate,” of gold and silver. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, regarding his statement: Say, ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’ he said: The grace of God is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur’an. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Zaid told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, regarding his statement: Say, ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’ he said: Islam and the Qur’an. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Hilal, the same. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice.’ As for His bounty, it is Islam, and as for His mercy, it is the Qur’an. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan: “Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy,” he said: His grace is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur’an. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Say, ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’ he said: the Qur’an. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And by His mercy, he said: the Qur’an. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement: It is better than what they accumulate, he said: Money and other things. Ali bin Dawud told us, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy,” meaning: His grace is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur’an. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice.’ He said: In the Book of God and in Islam, that is better than what they accumulate. Others said: Rather, the virtue is the Qur’an, and mercy is Islam. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: “Say: By the grace of God and His mercy - in that let them rejoice. It is better than what they accumulate,” he said: By the grace of God, the Qur’an, and by His mercy, when He made them among the people of the Qur’an. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ja`far bin `Awn told us, he said, Hisham bin Sa`d told us, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, he said: The grace of God is the Qur’an, and His mercy is Islam. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Say, ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’ he said: By the grace of God, the Qur’an, and by His mercy, Islam. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement: “Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy - in that let them rejoice,” he said: My father used to say: His grace is the Qur’an, and His mercy is Islam. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: So let them rejoice in that. So the majority of the reciters of the regions read it: So let them rejoice with the letter ya “It is better than what they accumulate” with the letter ya also, according to the interpretation that we have interpreted, that it is report about the people of polytheism with God. He says: So let these polytheists rejoice with Islam and the Qur’an to which he called them, not with the money that they accumulate, for Islam and the Qur’an are better than the money that they accumulate. And likewise: It was narrated on the authority of Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayyah: “So let them rejoice in that. It is better than what they accumulate,” meaning the infidels. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab regarding this matter: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Aslam Al-Manqari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abza, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b: that he used to recite: “So in that let you rejoice. It is better than what you accumulate,” with the letter ta’. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abza, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, the same. And likewise, Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to say: However, what was mentioned about him was that he used to read his statement: It is better than what they collect, with the letter ya, the first as a direct address, and the second as a report about the absent. Abu Jaafar Al-Qari, as mentioned about him, used to read it similarly to Abu’s reading, with both the letter ta’ and the letter ‘ta’. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in this regard is what the regions read, which is to read both letters together with a ya’: So let them rejoice, it is better than what they accumulate, for two meanings: One of them: the consensus of the argument from the recitation on it. The second: It is correct in Arabic, as the Arabs hardly ever command the addressee with the letter lam and the letter ta, but rather they command him and say: Do and do not do. And then, I do not know of any of the Arabs who does not reject the command of the one addressed by the lam, and sees that it is a language that is not desired, except for al-Farra’, who used to claim that the lam in the imperative is the structure for which it was created, whether you confront it or not, except that the Arabs deleted the lam from the verb of the one being confronted, due to the frequency of the command in their speech, especially as they deleted the ta’ from the verb. He said: And you know that the jussive and the nasib only occur with the verb that begins with the ya’, the ta’, the nun, and the alif, so when the ta’ was deleted, the lam was lost, and the alif was introduced in your saying: (idrib) and (ifrah), because the fa’ is silent, so it was not right to start over with a silent letter, so they introduced a light alif with which to start, as he said: (idrakū) (al-A’raf 7:38) and (ataqaltum) (al-Tawbah 9:38). This is what Al-Farraa’ relied on, not for him. That is because if the Arabs had deleted the lam in the word muwajih and left it out, then no one else, when he speaks their language, has the right to include in it what is not from it, as long as he speaks in their language. If he did that, he would be outside their language. And the Book of God that He revealed to Muhammad is in their language, so no one has the right to recite it except in the most eloquent of their speech, even if some of that is known from the language of some of them, so how about what is not known from the language of a tribe or a tribe from it? It is only a claim that cannot be proven with evidence or validity.
10:59: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists, Have you considered, O people, what God has sent down for you of provision, meaning: what God created for you of provision and gave it to you, and that is what you eat of food, and you made of it unlawful and lawful, meaning: you made some of it lawful for yourselves, and made some of it unlawful for them, and that is like their unlawfulness of what they used to unlawful of their crops which they used to make for their idols, as God described them when He said: And they assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock, and said, ‘This is for God,’ according to their claim, and this is for our partners. (Al-An`am: 136) Among the livestock were those which they forbade by means of excessive slaughtering, letting it go, and the like, as we have presented previously in this book. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, Has God permitted you to forbid what you have forbidden, or do you invent falsehoods against God? That is, do you say falsehood and lie? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The people of ignorance used to forbid things that God had permitted, such as clothing and other things. This is what God said: Say, ‘Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, but you made some of it lawful and some unlawful?’ This is what God revealed: Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants?’ (al-A’raf 7:32). Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Say, ‘Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, then you made…’ to his statement: Or do you invent lies about God? He said: They are the people of polytheism. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And you made of it lawful and unlawful, he said: The crops and livestock. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: The lakes and the seeb. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you made of it what is forbidden and what is permissible, he said: In the Bahirah and the Sa’ibah. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Say, ‘Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it lawful and unlawful?’ The Verse, he says: Every provision that I have not forbidden, you have forbidden to yourselves of your women, your wealth, and your children. Has God given you permission to do what you have forbidden of that, or do you invent lies about God? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Say, ‘Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it lawful and unlawful?’ So he recited until he reached: Or do you invent lies about God? And he recited: And they say, ‘What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives’ (Al-An`am 6:139), and he recited: And they say, ‘These are livestock and tillage that are forbidden.’ Until he reached: They do not mention the name of God over them (Al-An`am 6:138). So he said: This is His statement, He made provision for them, and they made of it lawful and unlawful, and they forbade some of it and made some of it lawful. And he recited: “Eight pairs of sheep, two of them, and two of the goats. Say: ‘Is it the two males He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?’” That is, these two are forbidden to those who say, and are permissible to those who say, Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful, or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you? to the end of the verses, (al-An’am 6:142-144). It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: “Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, but you have made of it lawful and unlawful?” He is the one about whom God said: And they have assigned to God a share of what He has created of crops and livestock until His statement: Evil is that which they judge (Al-An`am: 136).
10:60: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: What do these people who fabricate lies against God, adding to them the prohibition of what He did not prohibit for them of provisions and sustenance which God made for them as food, think that God will deal with them on the Day of Resurrection because of their lies and slander against Him? Do they think that He will pardon them and forgive them? No, rather He will burn them in a blazing fire wherein they will abide forever. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, meaning that God is full of bounty to His creation, by not hastening to punish those who fabricated lies against Him in this world, and by giving them respite until it comes to Him on the Day of Resurrection. But most of them are not grateful, meaning that most people do not thank Him for His bounty to them with this and other blessings of His.
10:61: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you are not, O Muhammad, in any affair, meaning: in any action, nor do you recite from it any Qur’an, meaning: what you recite from the Book of God from the Qur’an, nor do you do any deed, meaning: and you do not do any good or evil from your life, O people, except that We are witnesses over you, meaning: except that We are witnesses to your actions and affairs, as you do them and take action in them. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the statement was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and a group. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: When you are pouring into it, he said: When you are doing. Others said: The meaning of this is that you spread lies in the Qur’an. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: When you spread lies in the Qur’an, meaning: you spread lies in the Qur’an. Others said that the meaning of this is: when you are overflowing with truth. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: When you are pouring forth therein, in the truth, whatever it was.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Ja`far said: We chose the statement that we chose about it because the Most High informed us that His servants do not do a deed except that He witnesses it, then He connected that with His statement: When you are pouring into it, so it was known that His statement: When you are pouring into it, is only a report from Him about the time of the work of the workers, that it has a witness, not about the time of the Prophet’s recitation of the Qur’an, because if that were a report about His witnessing the time of the people pouring into the Qur’an, then the reading with the letter ya’ would be: (When you are pouring into it), a report from Him about those who deny it. If someone says: This is not report about the deniers, but rather it is an address to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he witnessed him when he recited the Qur’an. If that were the case, the revelation would have been: When you pour it out, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one, not a group, as He said: And whatever you recite of the Qur’an, so He singled him out in the address, but that is in his beginning his address to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the individual, then his returning to directing the address to the group, similar to his saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1), and that is because in his saying: When you divorce women, there is clear evidence that he directed the address to the group of Muslims with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a group of people other than him, because he began his address, then directed the address to the group of people and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them. And the report that none of His servants does a deed except that He witnesses it, counts it and knows it, as He said: And nothing is hidden from your Lord, O Muhammad, the work of His creation, and the knowledge of anything does not escape Him, whether it is on earth or in heaven. Its origin is from (the man’s absence from his family in his livestock), which means his absence from them in it. It is said from it: (the man was absent from his family, he is absent and absent). Two eloquent languages, each of which was read by a group of reciters, and whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct, because their meanings are the same, and they are widespread in the language of the Arabs. However, I tend towards the damma in it, because it is more common among the famous reciters. His saying: From the weight of an atom, means: from the weight of a small ant. It is said about the Arabs: (Take this, for it is a mithqal lighter than that), meaning: lighter in weight. The word atom is one: dhar, and dhar is the small ant. Abu Ja`far said: This is report that nothing is hidden from Him, glory be to Him, the smallest of things, even if they are extremely light in weight, and their amounts and their extent, nor is the largest of them, even if they are great and heavy in weight, and their extent. God Almighty says to His creation: Let your work, O people, be in that which pleases your Lord, for We are witnesses to your deeds, nothing of them is hidden from Us, and We are their recorders and rewarders. The readings differed in the reading of his saying: nor smaller than that nor larger. The majority of readers read it with the opening of the ra of asghar and akbar, on the basis that its meaning is lowering, in apposition to asghar for atoms, and akbar for asghar, then their ra was opened, because they do not run. Some of the Kufians read it as: (nor smaller than that nor greater), in the nominative case, in apposition to the meaning of (the weight), because its meaning is the nominative case. This is because if (min) were dropped from the speech, (the weight) would be raised, and the speech would then be: (And nothing is hidden from your Lord, even the weight of an atom, nor smaller than the weight of an atom, nor greater), and this is similar to His statement: Who is a creator other than God and other than God (Fatir 35:3). Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads with the fat-ha, in the manner of lowering and returning to the atom, because that is the reading of the people of the regions, and the common people of the reading are upon it, and it is more correct in Arabic in terms of its articulation, even though the other has a well-known aspect. And His statement: Except in a clear Book, meaning: And all of that is only in a Book with God, clear, about the truth of God’s report for whoever looks into it, that nothing was or will be except that God, may His praise be glorified, has counted it in it, and that nothing of His creation is hidden from God, wherever it may be, from His heavens and His earth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And it does not escape, meaning: it does not disappear from Him. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And nothing is hidden from your Lord, he said: What is absent from Him.
10:62: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Except that the supporters of God will have no fear in the Hereafter from God’s punishment, because God was pleased with them and made them safe from His punishment, nor will they grieve over what they missed of this world. And al-Awliya is the plural of wali, which means supporter, and we have explained that with its evidence. The interpreters differed about who deserves this name. Some of them said: They are a people whom God remembers when they are seen, because of their good and humble characteristics. Who said that? Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Behold, the allies of God have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve, he said: Those whom God is remembered for seeing.
