Abu Kuraib and Abu Hisham told us, they said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father: Behold, the friends of God have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve. He said: Those whom God is remembered for seeing.... He said, Ibn Mahdi and Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, who said: I heard him say about this verse: Behold, for the allies of God there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve. He said: Among the people are keys, when they see God, they are remembered for seeing them.... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Sahl Abi al-Asad, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ‘the friends of God,’ and he said: ‘Those who, when they are seen, remember God.’”... He said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah: Behold, the friends of God have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve. He said: Those who, when they see, God is remembered for seeing them.... He said, Abu Yazid al-Razi told us, on the authority of Yaqub, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: They are those who, when they see God mentioned. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Furat told us, on the authority of Abu Sa`d, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ‘the friends of God.’ He said: They are those who, when they see God, are remembered.”... He said, Al-Husayn told us, Hisham told us, Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, regarding his statement: Unquestionably, for the allies of God there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve, the verse, he said: When the allies of God are seen, God is remembered. Others said about this: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i narrated, he said: Ibn Fadil narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of ‘Ammarah ibn Al-Qa’qa’ Ad-Dhabi, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah ibn ‘Amr ibn Jarir Al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Among the servants of God are servants whom the prophets and martyrs envy!’ It was said: ‘Who are they, O Messenger of God? Perhaps we will love them!’ He said: ‘They are people who love one another for the sake of God, without wealth or lineage. Their faces are of light, upon pulpits of light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve except when people grieve.’” And he recited: Behold, the friends of God have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Ammarah, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Among the servants of God are people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, but the prophets and martyrs will envy them on the Day of Resurrection because of their status with God!’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell us who they are and what their deeds are?’ For that is why we love them! He said: ‘They are people who love one another for the sake of God, with the spirit of God, without any kinship ties between them or money that they exchange. By God, their faces are radiant, and they are upon light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve.’ And he recited this verse: ‘Unquestionably, for the friends of God there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve.’” Bahr bin Nasr Al-Khawlani told us, Yahya bin Hassan told us, Abdul Hamid bin Bahram told us, Shahr bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Ghanam, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There will come from the depths of the people and the conflicts of the tribes, a people who have not maintained close kinship ties, but who loved one another for the sake of God and were united for the sake of God. God will place for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, and He will seat them on them. People will be terrified but they will not be terrified, and they will be the friends of God who will have no fear, nor will they grieve.” Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this is: The wali - I mean the wali of God - is the one who has the attribute that God described him with, and he is the one who believed and feared God, as God said: Those who believed and were fearing God. Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we said about that. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Unquestionably, the allies of God have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve, who are they, O Lord? He said: Those who believed and were fearing God, my father said: Faith will not be accepted except through fearing God.
10:63: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Those who believed in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God, and they feared God by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. His saying: Those who believed, is an attribute of the friends, and the meaning of the statement is: Indeed, the friends of God who believed and were righteous, there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve. If someone says: If the meaning of the speech is what you mentioned, is those who believed in the nominative case, or in the accusative case? It was said: In the nominative case. And it was thus, even though it was an attribute of (the saints), because it came after the predicate of (the saints), and the Arabs do this especially with (in), if the attribute of the noun that it worked on came after the completion of its predicate, they raise it and say: (Indeed your brother is standing, the elegant), as God said: “Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the truth, Knower of the unseen” (Saba’ 34:48), and as He said: “Indeed, that is the truth. The dispute of the people of the Fire” (Sad 38:64). The Arab scholars differed on the reason why this was said thus, although they all agreed that what we have said is the correct speech of the Arabs. This is not one of the places to clarify the reasons why this was said thus.
10:64: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Good tidings from God in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, for the friends of God who believed and were righteous. Then the people of interpretation differed about the good report that God gave these people. What is it? And what is its description? Some of them said: It is a righteous vision that a Muslim man sees or that is seen for him, and in the hereafter it is Paradise. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Dhakwan, on the authority of a sheikh, “on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A righteous dream that a believer sees or that is seen for him.’” Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Al-Awza’i told us, he said, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, he said, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman told me, he said: “Ubadah bin As-Samit asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: ‘Those who believe and fear God, for them are good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have asked me about something that no one before you has asked me about - or he said: other than you - he said: It is the righteous vision that a righteous man sees or is seen.” Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God Almighty: ‘Those who believe and fear God - for them are good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter’, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is a righteous vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him.” Abu Qilabah told us, he said, Muslim told us, he said, Aban told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Muslimah, on the authority of Ubadah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Abu Uthman bin Omar told us, they said, Ali bin Yahya told us, “On the authority of Abu Salamah, he said: I was informed that Ubadah bin Al-Samit asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’ He said: You asked me about something that no one before you asked me about. It is the good dream that a man sees or that is seen for him.” Abu al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from the people of Egypt, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’: For them is good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. He said: “A man asked Abu al-Darda’ about this verse, and he said: You have asked me about something that I have not heard anyone ask about after a man asked about it the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is a righteous vision that a Muslim man sees or that is seen for him, good tidings for him in this worldly life, and good tidings for him in the Hereafter are Paradise.” Sa`id ibn `Umar al-Sakuni told me, he said, `Uthman ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadhir, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from Egypt who said: I asked Abu al-Darda` about this verse: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. He said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except you, except one man! I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: No one has asked me about it that God revealed except you, except one man. It is the good dream that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him. Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Munkadir, he heard Ata bin Yasar telling, on the authority of a man from the people of Egypt: that he asked Abu Al-Darda’ about: They will have good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni, on the authority of Uthman bin Saeed. Abu Hamid al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Ahmoosi narrated to us, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, he said: “A man came to Ubadah ibn al-Samit and said: There is a verse in the Book of God that I should ask you about, the statement of God: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter’? Ubadah said: No one asked me about it before you. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and he said the same: No one asked me about it before you! The righteous vision is seen by the believing servant in a dream or it is seen for him.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Bakr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A good dream is good report, which a Muslim sees or which is seen for him.... He said, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said, Abu Hurairah said: The good vision is good report from God, and it is the good report. Muhammad bin Hatim Al-Mu’addab told us, he said, Ammar bin Muhammad told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: They will have good tidings in this worldly life, the righteous vision that the righteous servant sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, he said, Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: They will have good tidings in this worldly life. A good dream, which gives the servant good tidings, is one of forty-nine parts of prophecy. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid bin Safwan, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: They will have good tidings in this world and in the Hereafter. We have learned the good tidings of the Hereafter, but what is the good tidings of this world? He said: A righteous vision that a servant sees or that is seen for him, and it is one part of forty-four parts - or sixty parts - of prophecy. Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abu Omar told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ubadah bin As-Samit: He asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: For them is good tidings in the life of this world, so he said: You have asked me about something that no one from my nation has asked me about before you! It is the righteous dream that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise. Ahmad bin Hammad Al-Dulabi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubaid God bin Abi Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saba’ bin Thabit, “on the authority of Umm Kurz Al-Ka’biyyah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Prophethood has gone, but the good tidings remain.” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhakwan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: For them is good tidings in the life of this world, he said: The righteous vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter, Paradise. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man who was in Egypt, he said: I asked Abu Darda’ about this verse: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. Abu Darda’ said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one has asked me about it before you. It is a good dream that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise.... He said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Salih, “On the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his saying: ‘For them is good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter.’ He said: No one asked me about it except you. It is a good dream that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him.”... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, “On the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ regarding his statement: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter,’ he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and he said: No one asked me about it before you. It is the righteous vision that a servant sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise.”... He said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi`, on the authority of Abu Salih - Ibn Uyaynah said: Then I heard it from Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman - on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, “on the authority of a man from the people of Egypt who said: I asked Abu al-Darda’ about this verse: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world’. He said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: No one has asked me about it since it was revealed to me except one man. It is the good dream that a man sees or that is seen for him.”... He said, Abdullah Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, on the authority of Hatim bin Abi Saghira, “On the authority of Amr bin Dinar: that he asked a man from the people of Egypt, a jurist, who came to them during one of those seasons, he said I said: Will you not tell me about the statement of God Almighty: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world’? He said: I asked Abu Al-Darda’ about it, and he informed me that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and he said: A good dream that a servant sees or that is seen for him.”... He said, my father told me, on the authority of Ali bin Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, “on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world.’ He said: It is a righteous vision that a servant sees or that is seen for him.” Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim and Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, they said, Aban told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, he said, I said: O Messenger of God, did God say: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter? He said: You have asked Me about something that no one before you has asked Me about - or: no one from my nation - He said: The righteous dream that a righteous man sees or that is seen for him.... He said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, “On the authority of Abu Salih, he said: I heard Abu Al-Darda’, and he was asked about “Those who believe and fear God - for them are good tidings in the life of this world.” He said: No one asked me about it before you since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: No one asked me about it before you! It is the righteous vision that a servant sees or that is seen for him.” Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, “on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world,’ he said: It is a good vision that a person sees or that is seen for him.”...And Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ - or Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, “On the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: It is the good dream.”...And Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said: It is a vision that a man sees. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, he said: It is the good vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father: They will have good tidings in this worldly life, he said: It is the righteous vision that the righteous servant sees.... He said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It is the righteous vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him.... He said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Talha al-Qannad, on the authority of Ja`far bin Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For them is good tidings in the life of this world. He said: It is the good vision that a Muslim servant sees for himself or for some of his brothers.... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: They used to say: A vision is one of the good tidings. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa`d: A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: No one from my nation has asked me about it since it was revealed to me before you! He said: It is a good dream that a man sees for himself or that is seen for him.... He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi: Ibn Masoud said: Prophethood has gone and the good tidings remain! It was said: What are the good tidings? He said: A good vision that a man sees or that is seen for him.... He said, Abdullah told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: For them is good tidings in the life of this world, it is his statement to his Prophet: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty (al-Ahzab 33:47). He said: It is the immediate vision that the believer sees or that is seen for him.... He said, Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Harb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: For them is good tidings in the life of this world, he said: It is a vision that a Muslim man is given in which he is given good tidings in his life. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Diraj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: They will have good tidings in this worldly life, the righteous vision that the believer is given good tidings of, is one of forty-six parts of prophecy. Yunus told me, he said, Anas bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, regarding this verse: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, he said: It is a good vision that a man sees or that is seen for him. Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Hamid ibn Abdullah told us: “A man asked Ubadah ibn al-Samit about the statement of God: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’ Ubadah said: ‘You have asked me about something that no one before you has asked me about, and I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what you asked me, and he said to me: ‘You have asked me about something that no one from my nation has asked me about!’ That is the righteous vision that a believer sees for himself or that is seen for him.” Others said: It is good report that the believer is given in this world at the time of death. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Qatada: For them is good tidings in the life of this world, he said: It is good tidings at death in the life of this world. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abu Bastam, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: They will have good tidings in the life of this world, he said: He will know where he is before death. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct interpretation of this is that God, the Most High, has informed us that His righteous friends will receive good tidings in this world. Among the good tidings in this worldly life is a righteous vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him, and among them is the good tidings of the angels to him when his soul departs with the mercy of God, as it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The angels who attend him when his soul departs say to his soul: ‘Come out to the mercy and pleasure of God.’” Among them is God’s good report to him, which He promised him in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the great reward, as He, the Most High, said: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow (al-Baqarah 2:25). All of these meanings are from God’s good tidings to him in this worldly life. He gave him good tidings of them. God did not specify one meaning over another, for that is what He, the Most High, has made general: For them is good tidings in this worldly life, and as for the Hereafter, it is Paradise. As for his saying: There is no changing the words of God, its meaning is that God does not break His promise, nor does He change what He said, but He fulfills His promises to His creation and accomplishes them for them. And: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’ who said: Al-Hajjaj prolonged the sermon, so Ibn Umar put his head on my lap. Al-Hajjaj said: Ibn al-Zubayr has changed the Book of God! Ibn Umar sat up and said: You cannot do that, nor can Ibn al-Zubayr! There is no changing the words of God! Al-Hajjaj said: You have been given knowledge if it benefits you! Ayoub said: When he turned to him in private, he was silent. And His statement: That is the great attainment, God Almighty says: This is good report of this worldly life and in the Hereafter, and it is the great attainment, meaning achieving one’s need and request and being saved from the Fire.
10:65: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not let the saying of these polytheists about their Lord, what they say, and their associating idols and statues with Him grieve you, for all glory belongs to God. God Almighty says: For God is the One who is alone in the glory of this world and the Hereafter, He has no partner in it, and He is the One who will take revenge on these polytheists who say what they say of falsehood about Him, so no one will help you when He takes revenge on them, because nothing can help Him. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, meaning: He is the One who hears what they say of slander and lies about Him, and He is the One who knows what they conceal in their souls and what they declare, counting all of that against them, and He is watching them. The word in was broken in his statement: Indeed, glory belongs to God entirely, because that is report from God as a subject, and the word speech did not work on it, because the word speech meant the saying of the polytheists, and his statement: Indeed, glory belongs to God entirely, was not said by the polytheists, nor is it report about them that they said it.
10:66: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Verily, O Muhammad, God has all that is in the heavens and on the earth, a king and slaves. There is no owner of any of that except Him. He says: How can the idols and statues that these polytheists worship be a god that is worshipped, while they belong to God, and worship is only for the owner and not the owned, and for the Lord and not the worshipped?, And those they invoke other than God do not follow partners, God Almighty says: And what does he follow who invokes other than God - meaning: other than God and other than Him - partners? The meaning of the statement: What would follow someone who falsely says that God has partners in His authority and kingdom, while God is the only One who owns everything in the heavens and the earth? They follow nothing but conjecture, meaning: they follow nothing in their saying and their claim except conjecture, meaning: nothing but doubt and certainty. They are only guessing, meaning: they are only inventing falsehood based on conjecture and guesswork, without knowledge of what they are saying.
10:67: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Your Lord, O people, who has made worship obligatory upon you, is the Lord who made the night for you and separated it from the day, so that you may rest in it from the fatigue and toil you were in during the day, and calm down in it from the movement and activity for livelihood, and the hardship you were in during the day, and the day is seeing, meaning: and He made the day seeing. So He added sight to day, and it is only seeing in it, and day is not among what is seen. But since its meaning was understood in the speech of the Arabs, He addressed them with what is in their language and speech, and that is as Jarir said: You blamed us, O Umm Ghilan, in the night and you slept, and the night of the mounts is not asleep So he added sleep to night and described it with it, and its meaning is the same, that neither he nor his camel was asleep in it. God Almighty says: This is the one who does that. He is your Lord who created you and what you worship, not what does not benefit or harm or do anything. And His statement: Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen, God Almighty says: Indeed in the difference in the state of night and day and the state of their people in them, there is evidence and proof that the One to whom worship is due, purely without partner, is the One who created the night and the day, and made them different by making this a resting place for creation, and this a livelihood for them, unlike the One who neither creates nor does anything, nor harms nor benefits. He said: For a people who listen, because what is meant by it is: those who hear these arguments and think about them, so they consider them and learn a lesson. It does not mean: those who hear with their ears, then turn away from its lessons and sermons.
10:68: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: These polytheists from your people said, O Muhammad: God has taken a son, and that is their saying: (The angels are daughters of God). God says, clearing Himself of what they said and fabricated about Him: (Glory be to God), clearing God of what they said and claimed against their Lord, He is the Rich, meaning: God is rich in relation to all of His creation, so He has no need for a son, because a son is only sought by those who seek Him, so that he may be a helper for them in their life, and a reminder for them after their death, and God is rich in all of that, so He has no need for a helper to assist him in his management, nor will He perish so that there would be a need for a successor after Him, To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, God Almighty says: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and the angels are His servants and His kingdom, so how can a man's servant and his kingdom be a son? He says: Do you not understand, O people, the error of what you are saying? You have an authority for this. He says: What evidence do you have, O people, for what you say and claim that the angels are daughters of God? Which is the authority. Do you say about God a statement whose truth and correctness you do not know, and do you attribute to Him what it is not permissible to attribute to Him, out of ignorance of what you are saying, without an argument or proof?
10:69: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them, Indeed, those who invent falsehood about God, by saying falsehood about Him and claiming a son for Him, will not succeed, meaning: they will not remain in this world.
10:70: But they have enjoyment in this world, and provision, with which they will attain until the appointed time for their demise has been decreed. Then to Us is their return, meaning, when the appointed time has come to an end, to Us is their destination and their final destination. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment, meaning they will be cast into Hell, because they disbelieved in God in this world, denying His messengers and rejecting His signs. He raised his saying: Provisions, with an implied word before it, either that or this.
10:71: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And recite, to these polytheists who said: God has taken a son from among your people, the report of Noah, meaning: the report of Noah, when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my stay among you is too much for you,' meaning: if my stay among you is too much for you and is difficult for you, and my reminding you of the signs of God, meaning: and my admonition to you of the proofs of God, and my alerting you to that, Then upon God I have put my trust, meaning: if my stay among you is too much for you, and my reminding you of the signs of God, and you decide to kill me or expel me from among you, then upon God I rely and in Him I trust, and He is my support and my back, Then decide your plan, meaning: then prepare your plan, and resolve on what you intend regarding my matter. It is said: I have resolved to do such-and-such, meaning: I have decided to do it. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever does not resolve to fast at night, then his fast is not valid, meaning: whoever does not resolve. From this is the saying of the poet: I wonder, for hopes are of no avail, will I ever become one day when my affair is resolved? It was narrated on the authority of Al-A’raj regarding this matter: Some of our companions told me, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Asid, on the authority of al-A’raj: So decide your matter and your partners, meaning: decide your matter and call your partners. And the accusative of his saying: and your partners, is an implied verb, which is: (and call your partners), and the conjunction of (the partners) to his saying (your matter), similar to the saying of the poet: I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. The spear is not girdled, but since what appeared in the speech was evidence of what was omitted, it was sufficient to mention what was mentioned of what was omitted, and so it is in His statement: (and your partners). There are different readings of this: So I read it as the regions read: And your partners, in the accusative case. And his saying: So they gathered, with a hamza on the alif and a fatha on it, from: (I gathered my affair, so I gather it unanimously). It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it: So gather your affair, with the alif open and hamzated, and your partners, in the nominative case, meaning: gather your affair, and let your partners gather their affair with you as well. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in this regard is the reading of those who read: So gather your affair and your partners, with the opening of the alif of agma`u and the accusative of al-sharakah, because it is in the Qur’an without a waw, and because of the consensus of the argument on reading it with it, and rejecting what contradicts it, and it cannot be objected to by those who are liable for error and forgetfulness. By partners, he meant their gods and idols. And his saying: Then let not your affair be a cause of grief for you, means: Then let not your affair be ambiguous, problematic, or unclear for you. From their saying: The crescent moon was obscure to the people, meaning if it was unclear to them and they could not see it. From this is the saying of Al-Ajjaj: Rather, if you witnessed people when they were filled with grief, their grief would not have been relieved. It was said: This is from sorrow, because the chest becomes tight with it, and its owner does not know the source of his matter from which it comes, and he is relieved of what is in his heart. From this is the saying of Khansa: And Dhi Karba, Ibn Amr relaxed his stranglehold and his grief from his face, so it was revealed. Qatada used to say about this: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Your affair is a burden upon you, he said: Your affair is not a burden upon you. As for the saying: Then proceed to me, its meaning is: Then proceed to what is in your souls and finish it, as: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then judge me and do not give me respite, he said: Judge me as you were going to judge. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Then judge me and do not give me respite, he said: Judge me what is in your souls. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Those who know the Arabic language differed about the meaning of his saying: Then come to me. Some of them said: It means: Go to me, just as one says: So-and-so has passed away, meaning: he has died and gone. Others of them said: Rather, its meaning is: Then, come to me. They said: The judgment means to finish, and the judgment is from that. They said: As if he paid off his debt is from that, but rather he finished with it. It has been narrated that some of the Qur’an reciters read it as: Then they came to me, meaning: head towards me until you reach me, from their saying: The pain and the like have come to me. And his saying: And do not wait, means: and do not delay. From the saying: I have given so-and-so respite for the debt he owes me. Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God, the Most High, about the words of His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, to his al-Nas 114:He is confident in God’s victory over them, and he is not afraid of their plots and their calamities. It is an announcement from Him to them that their gods can neither harm nor benefit. He says to them: Carry out what you tell yourselves about me, with a sound resolve from you, and seek help with those who support you against me through your gods that you call upon besides God, and do not delay that, for I have put my trust in God, and I am confident in Him that you will not harm me unless my Lord wills. This, even though it is report from God Almighty about Noah, is an urging from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to follow his example, and an explanation from him of the path of guidance in what he was entrusted with of the message and the delivery of it from him.
10:72: The Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, said to his al-Nas 114:If you turn away, O people, from me after I have called you and conveyed the message of my Lord to you, turning away, and turning away from what I have called you to of the truth, and the acknowledgment of the oneness of God, and the sincerity of worship to Him, and the abandonment of associating deities in His worship, then this is a waste on your part and a neglect of the duty of God’s right over you, not because of anything on my part, for I have not asked you for what I have called you to a reward, nor a compensation that I could exchange from you for your response to what I have called you to of the truth and guidance, nor have I asked you for a reward or recompense for it, My reward is only with God, the Almighty says: My reward and the reward of my work and its recompense are only with my Lord, not upon you, O people, nor upon anyone else, And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, and my Lord has commanded me to be among those who submit to Him in obedience, who are submissive. To His command and prohibition, submissive to Him. And for that reason I call you to Him, and by His command I command you to abandon the worship of idols.
10:73: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Noah's people denied what he told them about God's message and revelation, So We saved him and those with him, those who were carried with him, in the ark, meaning: in the ship, and made them successors, meaning: We made those who were saved with Noah in the ship, successors on the earth from his people who denied him, after We drowned those who denied Our signs, meaning: Our arguments and proofs of Our Oneness and the message of Our Messenger Noah. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: So see, O Muhammad, how was the end of those who were warned, and they are those whom Noah warned of God's punishment for denying him and worshipping idols. God Almighty says to him: Look at what happened to them after they denied their Messenger. The consequence of those among your people who denied you, if they persist in their disbelief and transgression against their Lord, is similar to what happened to the people of Noah when they denied him. God Almighty says: Let them beware that what happened to them will happen to them if they do not repent.
10:74: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Then We sent after Noah messengers to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs and evidence of their truthfulness, and that they are messengers of God, and that what they call them to is true, But they were not to believe in what they denied before, meaning: They were not to believe in what their messengers brought them, in what the people of Noah and the nations before them denied. Thus do We set a seal upon the hearts of the transgressors, meaning: Just as We set a seal upon the hearts of those, so that they would not accept the advice of God's prophets, nor would they respond to their call to their Lord, because of the sins they committed and the crimes they acquired, thus do We set a seal upon the hearts of those who transgressed against their Lord, so they transgressed what He commanded them to do of His Oneness, and opposed what their messengers called them to do of obeying Him, as a punishment for their disobedience to their Lord from among those who came after them.
10:75: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Then We sent, after the messengers whom We sent after Noah to their people, Moses and Aaron, the sons of Imran, to Pharaoh of Egypt and his people, meaning: and the nobles and leaders of his people, with Our signs, meaning: with Our evidence of the truth of what they called them to of submission to God in worship, and acknowledging their message to them, but they were arrogant, meaning: they were arrogant about acknowledging what Moses and Aaron called them to, and they were a criminal people, meaning: sinful towards their Lord, by their disbelief in God.
10:76: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So when the truth came to them from Us, meaning: When the explanation of what Moses and Aaron called them to came to them, and that was the arguments they brought to them, which were the truth that came to them from God, they said, ‘This is obvious magic,’ meaning that it was clear to whoever saw it and witnessed it that it was magic that had no reality.
10:77: Moses said, to them, Do you say of the truth that has come to you, from God, Is this magic? The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the interrogative letter alif being used in the phrase Is this magic? Some of the Basra grammarians said: I included it in the narrative because of their saying, because they said: Is this magic? So he said: Do you say: Is this magic? Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: They said: (This is magic), and they did not say it with an alif, because most of what came without an alif. He said: It is said: Why did you include the alif? It is said: It may be possible that it was said by them while they knew that it was magic, as a man says to a prize when it comes to him: (Is this true)? And he knows that it is true. He said: It may be possible that it was out of amazement from them: Is this magic? How great it is! Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these things in my opinion is that the object is omitted, and his saying, Is this magic? is from Moses, denying Pharaoh and his people’s saying about the truth when it came to them: magic. So the interpretation of the statement then is: Moses said to them: Do you say about the truth when it came to you - and they are the signs that he brought to them from God as proof of his truthfulness - magic. Is this the truth that you see magic? So the first magic is omitted, and it is sufficient to indicate that Moses’ saying, Is this magic, is intended in the statement, as Dhu al-Rummah said: When they got dressed for the night, or when it was time, she raised her ears to him while he was leaning forward. He means: or when he came, then he deleted it, being satisfied with the indication of the speech on it, and as God Almighty said: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will disfigure your faces (al-Isra’ 17:7), and the meaning is: We sent them to disfigure your faces, so he left that out, being satisfied with the indication of the speech on it, in many similarities to what we mentioned, it is difficult to count them. And His saying: And the magicians will not succeed, means: And the magicians will not succeed and will not remain.
10:78: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Pharaoh and his chiefs said to Moses: Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers upon, meaning: to divert and distort us, from the religion we found our fathers upon, before your coming. It is said: So-and-so twisted so-and-so’s neck, if he twisted it, as Ru’bah said: Turnip and tahzee’ both (Al-Tahzee’), Al-Daq, and (Al-Laft), Al-Li, as: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: To turn us away, he said: To turn us away from what we found our fathers upon. His saying: And you will have pride on earth, meaning greatness, which is the fa’liya from al-kabr, and from it is the saying of Ibn al-Ruqa’: A leadership that is not excessive, without arrogance or haughtiness Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you will have pride on the earth, he said: the kingdom.... He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid: And you will have pride on earth, he said: authority on earth.... He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: It was reported to me on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The king is on earth.... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And you will have pride on earth, he said: Obedience. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you will have pride on the earth, he said: the kingdom.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The authority on earth. Abu Jaafar said: All of these sayings have similar meanings. That is because kingship is authority, and obedience is authority. However, the meaning of pride, which is what is established in the speech of the Arabs, is that it is greatness through kingship and authority and other things. And His statement: And we are not believers in you, means: And we are not believers in you, O Moses and Aaron, “meaning: we will acknowledge that you are two messengers sent to us.”
10:79: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And Pharaoh said to his al-Nas 114:Bring me every magician who practices magic, who is knowledgeable in magic.
10:80: So when the magicians came, Pharaoh, Moses said to them, 'Cast down what you are casting down,' of your ropes and your staffs. There is something omitted in the speech that was left out, which is: (So they brought him the magicians, and when the magicians came), but I am satisfied with the indication of his saying: And when the magicians came, on that, so I left mentioning it. Likewise, after his saying: Throw down what you are going to throw down, something is also omitted and its mention was left out, which is: (So they threw down their ropes and their staffs). So when they threw down, Moses said, but he was satisfied with the indication of what appeared from the speech on it, so he left mentioning it.
10:81: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: So when they threw down what they were going to throw down, Moses said to them: What you have brought is magic. The readers differed in reading that. The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: What you have brought is magic, as a report from Moses about what Pharaoh’s magicians brought, that it was magic. It is as if the meaning of the speech according to their interpretation is: Moses said: What you have brought, you magicians, is magic. Mujahid and some of the Medinans and Basrans read it as: What you have brought is magic, as a question from Moses to the magicians about what they brought: Is it magic or something else? Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it as a statement, not as a question, because Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, did not doubt that what the magicians had brought was magic that had no reality, so he needed to ask the magicians about it, what it was. Another is that he, may God’s prayers be upon him, knew that the magicians had only brought them to Pharaoh to defeat him in what he had brought to them of the truth that God had given him. It did not escape him that they did not believe him in the report of what they had brought to him of falsehood, so he would ask them for information or permit them to ask him about it. But he, may God’s prayers be upon him, informed them that he knew of the invalidity of what they had brought of the truth that he had brought, and that he would nullify their plot with his own eyes. This is more appropriate for the description of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, than the other. If someone were to say: What is the reason for the inclusion of the definite article in magic if the matter is as you have described, and you know that the speech of the Arabs in a similar manner is that they say: What Umar brought me was a dirham, and what your brother gave me was a dinar, and they hardly ever say: What your brother gave me was a dirham, and what Amr brought me was a dinar? It was said to him: Yes, the speech of the Arabs is to insert (alif and lam) in the predicate of (ma) and (alladhi), if the predicate is about something known to the addressee and the addressee, rather it is not permissible if that is the case except with (alif and lam), because the predicate in that case is predicate about something specific known to both groups, and that only comes without (alif and lam), if the predicate is about an unknown that is not known and the intention is not to intend something specific, then in that case the alif and lam do not enter in the predicate. And the predicate of Moses was predicate about something known to him and to the magicians. That is because they attributed what Moses brought to them of the signs that God made a sign for him of his truthfulness and prophethood, to the fact that it was magic, so Moses said to them: The magic with which you described the signs that I brought to you, O magicians, is what you brought, not what I brought to you. Then he informed them that God would invalidate it, so he said: God will invalidate it, meaning: He will take it away. So God Almighty took him, by sending upon him the staff of Moses, which he had turned into a snake to swallow him, until nothing of him remained. Indeed, God does not amend the work of corrupters, meaning: He does not amend the work of one who strives in God’s land with what He hates, and commits sins therein. It was mentioned that this was in the reading of Abi bin Kaab: What you have brought is magic. In Ibn Masoud’s reading: What you have brought is magic, and this supports the reading of those who read in the manner we chose from the reading in it.
10:82: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about Moses that he said to the magicians: And God will establish the truth, meaning: And God will establish the truth that I have brought to you from Him, and will raise it above your falsehood and correct it, with His words, meaning: with His command, even though the criminals hate it, meaning: those who have acquired sin through their Lord, through their disobedience to Him.
10:83: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: No one believed in Moses, despite the arguments and evidence he brought them, except a few of his people, fearing Pharaoh and his people. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of offspring in this place. Some of them said: The offspring in this context means a small number. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And none believed in Moses except a few of his people, he said, Ibn Abbas used to say: The few. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding the words of God Almighty: And none believed in Moses except a few of his people, “the few,” as God Almighty said: just as He created you from the descendants of another people, (al-An’am 6:133). Others said: The meaning of this is: None believed in Moses except the descendants of those to whom Moses was sent from the Children of Israel, due to the length of time, because the fathers died and the sons remained, so they were called: descendants, because they were the descendants of those who perished from those to whom Moses, peace be upon him, was sent. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: None believed in Moses except the offspring of his people, he said: The children of those to whom he was sent for a long time, and their fathers had died. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: None believed in Moses except the offspring of his people, he said: The children of those to whom Moses was sent, due to the length of time, and their fathers had died. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash: None believed in Moses except a few of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, that he would tempt them. He said: The children of those to whom he was sent, and time passed over them, and their fathers died. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: None believed in Moses except the offspring of Pharaoh’s people. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And none believed in Moses except a few of his people, for fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, lest he should persecute them. He said: The offspring who believed in Moses were from people other than the Children of Israel, from Pharaoh’s people, a few of them: Pharaoh’s wife, a believer from Pharaoh’s family, Pharaoh’s treasurer, and his treasurer’s wife. A report was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that indicates the opposite of this statement, and that is: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: A descendants of his people, meaning: the Children of Israel. This report ofdicates that he believed that the offspring in this context were the Children of Israel, not the rest of Pharaoh’s people. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion regarding the interpretation of the verse is the saying that I mentioned on the authority of Mujahid, which is that the offspring in this place refers to the offspring of those to whom Moses was sent from the Children of Israel, but they perished before they acknowledged his prophethood due to the length of time, so their offspring lived, and those of them who remembered God believed in Moses. I said: This statement is more correct in this regard, because in this verse no one other than Moses is mentioned. So the ha in His statement: of his people is more likely to be from the mention of Moses, due to its proximity to his mention, than it is from the mention of Pharaoh, due to his being far from it, since there is no evidence to the contrary from a report or consideration. And then, in his saying: for fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, there is clear evidence that the ha in his saying: except for the offspring of his people, is from the mention of Moses, not from the mention of Pharaoh, because if it were from the mention of Pharaoh, the statement would have been, for fear of him, and it would not have been: for fear of Pharaoh. As for his saying: in fear of Pharaoh, he means in a state of fear of those who believed from the descendants of Moses’ people in Moses. The interpretation of the statement is: None believed in Moses except the descendants of his people from the Children of Israel, and they were afraid of Pharaoh and his chiefs that they would tempt them. Some Arabists have claimed that it was said: None believed in Moses except the offspring of his people, because those who believed in him had mothers from the Children of Israel and fathers from the Copts, so they were called offspring for that reason, just as the sons of the Persians whose mothers were Arabs and whose fathers were Persians were called sons. The meaning of offspring in the speech of the Arabs is known to be the descendants of those to whom they were attributed before, men and women, as God Almighty said: The descendants of those We carried with Noah (al-Isra’ 17:3), and as He said: And among his descendants were David, Solomon, Job, and Joseph, then He said after: And Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Elias (al-An’am 6:84, 85), so He made those who were before men and women from the descendants of Abraham. As for his saying: and their chiefs, “chiefs” are the nobles. The interpretation of the statement is: out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs. The Arabists differed as to who was meant by the ha and meem in his statement: and their chiefs. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He meant the offspring. It is as if he directed the speech to: And none believed in Moses except a few offspring from his people, out of fear of Pharaoh, and the chiefs were the offspring of the Children of Israel. Some grammarians of Kufa said: By them he meant Pharaoh. He said: This is permissible, and Pharaoh is one, because when a king is mentioned in fear, travel, or returning from a journey, the imagination goes to him and to those with him. He said: Don’t you see that you say: (The caliph arrived and the people increased), meaning those with him, (and he arrived and prices rose), because you mean by his arrival the arrival of those with him. He said: It may be that by (Pharaoh) you mean the family of Pharaoh, and you delete (the family), so it is permissible as he said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), meaning the people of the town, and God knows best. He said: Similar to it is his saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period (al-Talaq 65:1). Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: (The ha and the mim) refer to (the offspring), and the meaning of the statement is that he is in fear of Pharaoh and the chiefs of the offspring, because there were among the offspring of the century to whom he was sent those whose father was Coptic and whose mother was Israelite. So whoever was like that among them, was with Pharaoh against Moses. His saying: that he might tempt them, means: The faith of those who believed from the descendants of Moses’ people was out of fear of Pharaoh, that he might tempt them with punishment, turning them away from their religion, and causing them to turn back from their faith and disbelieve in God. He said: That he might tempt them, so he used the singular form, and did not say: that he might tempt them, because of the evidence of the report about Pharaoh in this regard: that his people were in the same state as he was in, because of what had been mentioned previously in his statement: in fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs. And His statement: And indeed, Pharaoh was arrogant in the land, God Almighty says: And indeed, Pharaoh was a tyrant, arrogant towards God in his land, and indeed, he was among the transgressors, and indeed, he was among those who transgressed the truth towards falsehood, and that was his disbelief in God, and his abandonment of belief in Him, and his denial of the oneness of God, and his claim for himself to be a god, and his shedding of blood unlawfully.
10:84: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Moses said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, if you have acknowledged the Oneness of God and believed in His Lordship, then put your trust in Him, meaning: So trust in Him, and submit to His command, for He will not let down His guardian, and he who puts his trust in Him will not be safe, if you are Muslims, meaning: If you are obedient to God, then put your trust in Him.
10:85: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Moses said to Moses: In God we trust, meaning: We trust in Him, and to Him we entrust our affairs. And His saying: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, God Almighty says, informing about the people of Moses: that they called upon their Lord and said: O our Lord, do not test these disbelieving people and do not try them with us, meaning the people of Pharaoh. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning that they asked their Lord for, of His protection from the affliction of Pharaoh’s people with them. Some of them said: They asked him not to make them prevail over them, lest they think that they were better than them, and that they were only given power over them because of their dignity in his eyes and the humiliation of others. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding his statement: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: So that they do not prevail over us, so that they see themselves as better than us. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding his statement: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: They said: Do not make them prevail over us, so that they see that they are better than us. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: Do not give them power over us, so that they become more tempted. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not let them rule over us so that they tempt us. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, do not give them power over us so that they tempt us. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: Do not give them power over us so that they lead us astray. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, and he also said: They tempt us. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, do not punish us at the hands of Pharaoh’s people, nor with a punishment from You, so that Pharaoh’s people say: If they were right, we would not have been given power over them nor would they have been punished, so that they would be tempted by us. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: Do not punish us at the hands of Pharaoh’s people or with a punishment from you, so that Pharaoh’s people say: If they were on the right path, we would not have been given power over them or punished, so that they would be tempted by us. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: Do not afflict us with a punishment from You or by their hands, so that they are tempted and say: If they were on the right path, We would not have been given power over them and they would not have been punished. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people, “Do not test us, our Lord, and exhaust us, and make it a trial for them, this trial.” And he recited: A trial for the wrongdoing people (37:63), he said: The polytheists, when they used to harm the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and the believers and throw stones at them, was that not a trial and evil for them, while it is a calamity for the believers? Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about that is that the people asked God to protect them from being a trial and a calamity for the people of Pharaoh. Everything that happened was a deterrent for them from following Moses and acknowledging him and what he brought to them. There is no doubt that it was a trial for them, and it was one of the greatest things that distanced them from faith in God and His Messenger. Likewise, one of the deterrents to faith was that if the people of Moses were suddenly a trial from God in themselves, from a calamity that would befall them, then the people sought refuge with God from every meaning that would prevent the people of Pharaoh from faith in God due to their causes.
10:86: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And save us, O our Lord, by Your mercy, so deliver us from the hands of the disbelieving people, the people of Pharaoh, because they were enslaving them and using them in the dirty things of their service.
10:87: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, Build houses for your people in Egypt. It is said: So-and-so made a house for himself, if he took it. Likewise: He made a house for himself, if he took it, And I made it a house for him, if he took it for himself. And make your homes places of prayer, meaning: And make your homes mosques in which you pray. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying: And make your homes places of prayer. Some of them said something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hameed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: mosques. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They were commanded to make them mosques.... He said, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail told us, he said, Zuhair told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They were afraid of Pharaoh and his people praying, so he said to them: (Make your houses places of prayer), meaning: Make them a mosque so that you may pray in them. Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And make your houses places of prayer. He said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And make your homes places of prayer. He said: They did not pray except in the shops, and they did not pray except in fear, so they were commanded to pray in their homes... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their homes... He said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: The Children of Israel feared Pharaoh, so they were commanded to make their houses mosques in which to pray. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, regarding his statement: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: mosques... He said, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They used to pray in their houses, fearing. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: That you provide houses for your people in Egypt, he said: mosques. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And make your houses places of prayer, he said: My father said: Make your houses your mosques in which you pray, that is (the qibla). Others said: Make your mosques before the Kaaba. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And make your houses places of prayer, meaning the Ka`bah. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And make your houses places of prayer and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers, he said: The Children of Israel said to Moses: We cannot openly pray with the Pharaohs! So God permitted them to pray in their houses, and they were commanded to make their houses places of prayer toward the Qiblah. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said, Ibn Abbas said regarding His statement: And make your houses places of worship, he said: Direct your houses, (your mosques), toward the qiblah. Do you not see that He says: In houses which God has permitted to be raised (al-Nur 24:36). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: And make your homes places of prayer, he said: before the prayer. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Your houses are a qiblah, he said: towards the Kaaba, when Moses and those with him feared that Pharaoh would pray in the congregational churches, so they were ordered to make mosques in their houses facing the Kaaba and to pray in them secretly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And make your homes places of prayer, then he mentioned something similar, the same.... He said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt,’ mosques.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: That you establish houses for your people in Egypt, he said: (Egypt), Alexandria. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And We inspired Moses and his brother, ‘Settle for your people in houses in Egypt and make your houses places of prayer. ’” He said: That was when Pharaoh prevented them from praying, so they were ordered to make their mosques in their houses, and to face the direction of the qibla. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Your houses are a qiblah, he said, towards the qiblah. Waki` told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt,’ he said: mosques, and make your houses places of prayer,’ he said: before the qiblah. Others said: The meaning of this is: Make your houses face each other. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And make your houses a qiblah, he said: facing one another. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one we have already explained, which is that the most common meaning of houses - even though mosques are houses - is inhabited houses, if mentioned by their absolute name, not mosques. Because mosques have a name by which they are known, specific to them, and that is mosques. As for houses in absolute terms without being connected to anything, or added to anything, they are inhabited houses. And also (Qiblah), people mostly use it in the direction of the mosques and for prayers. If this is the case, and it is not permissible to direct the meanings of God’s words except to the most common of their aspects, used by the people of the language in which it was revealed, without the hidden and unknown, unless there is evidence to the contrary, and there is no evidence for His statement: And make your houses places of prayer, which cuts off the excuse that its meaning is not the apparent one used in the speech of the Arabs, then it is not permissible for us to direct it to other than the apparent one that we have described. The same applies to his saying, kiss. “And establish prayer,” God Almighty says: And perform the obligatory prayer within its limits and at its times. And His saying: And give good tidings to the believers, God Almighty says to His Prophet, peace be upon him: And give good tidings to those who establish prayer, who obey God, O Muhammad, the believers, with the great reward from Him.
10:88: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And Moses said: O our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and the leaders and nobles of his people - who are the elites - adornment of worldly goods and furnishings, and wealth of gold and silver, in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way. Moses says to his Lord: Our Lord, You have given them what You have given them of that, so that they may go astray from Your way. There are different readings of this. Some of them read it as: So that they may lead people astray from Your path, meaning: so that they may lead people astray from Your path and turn them away from Your religion. Others read it as: So that they may go astray from Your path, meaning: So that they may go astray from Your path, and deviate from the path of guidance. If someone were to say: Did God, may He be glorified, give Pharaoh and his people what He gave them of worldly adornments and wealth, in order to lead people astray from His religion - or: in order for them to be led astray from it? If that was the reason He gave them that, then what He gave them was from them for that reason, so there is no blame on them for that?
