It was said: The meaning of this is different from what you imagined. The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the meaning of this lam in His statement: li-yidaloo. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is: Our Lord, they have strayed from Your path, as He said: So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a cause of grief (al-Qasas 28:8), meaning: So he was for them, and they did not pick him up so that he might become for them an enemy and a cause of grief, but rather they picked him up so that he was for them. He said: This lam comes in this meaning. Some Kufa grammarians said: This lam is lam ki, and the meaning of the statement is: Our Lord, You gave them what You gave them, so that they would go astray, then He invoked against them. Another said: These lams in His statement: to lead them astray, “to be an enemy to them” (al-Qasas 28:8), and what is similar to them is the interpretation of the khafd: I gave them what I gave them because of their misguidance - and they picked it up because of it - because the situation had come to that. The Arabs make (lam ki) in the meaning of (lam al-khafd) and (lam al-khafd) in the meaning of (lam ki), to make the meaning similar. God Almighty said: They will swear to you by God when you return to them to turn away from them (al-Tawbah 9:95): meaning: because of your turning away, and they did not swear because of their turning away. The poet said: You were exalted and you were not worthy of being exalted, but the lost may be afflicted He said: It is only said: (And you were not worthy of the action), and it is not said: (To do), except rarely. He said: This is from it. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in my opinion is that it is lam-ki, and the meaning of the statement is: Our Lord, You gave them what You gave them of the adornments of worldly life and wealth in order to tempt them with it, and to lead Your servants astray from Your path, as a punishment from You. This is as the Most High said: We would have certainly given them abundant water to test them thereby (al-Jinn 72:16-17). And his saying: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, this is a supplication from Moses, he supplicated to God against Pharaoh and his people to change their wealth from its form, and to change it to a state other than the one in which it is, and this is similar to his saying: Before We obliterate faces and turn them back, (An-Nisa’: 47), meaning by it: before We change it from the form in which it is. It is said: (He blinded his eye, I blind it, and I blinded it, blinding and blinding). The Arabs may use (blinding) to mean forgiveness and covering, and to crush and destroy, as Ka`b ibn Zuhair said: From every freshness of the penis, if it sweats, its display is obscured by the unknown flags The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this in this place. A group of them said the same thing about it as we said. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahra bin Zaida told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, he said: It has reached us on the authority of Al-Qurazi regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: Turn their sugar into stones. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, who said: Make their drunkenness stones. Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: Destroy their wealth, he said: Turn it into stones. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, regarding his statement: Destroy their wealth, he said: It turned into stones. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: We were informed that their crops were turned into stones. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: We were informed that their crops had turned into stones. Al-Muthanna told us, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, Sufyan told us: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: They say: It has become stones. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya Al-Hammani told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said it turned into stones. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: It has reached us that their crops have turned into stones. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, that God made it into engraved stones in the form in which it was. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: He did that, and that happened to them. He obliterated their wealth and it became stones, their gold, their dirhams, their lentils, and everything. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He destroyed it. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth. He said: Destroy it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, meaning: destroy them and annihilate their wealth. As for his saying: And harden their hearts, he means: And seal them so that they do not soften or expand with faith, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And Moses said before he came to Pharaoh: Our Lord, harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. So God answered him, and prevented Pharaoh from believing until he was drowned, so faith did not benefit him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And harden their hearts, he says: And seal their hearts, until they see the painful punishment, which is drowning. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And harden their hearts, with misguidance.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And harden their hearts, he said: with misguidance. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And harden their hearts, meaning: He destroyed them as disbelievers. As for his saying: They will not believe until they see the painful punishment, its meaning is: They will not believe in the oneness of God and acknowledge His oneness until they see the painful punishment, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They will not believe in God, in what they see of the signs, until they see the painful punishment. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.... He said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, I heard Al-Manqari say: So they will not believe, he said: He called down curses upon them. The Arabs differed about the position of believe. Some Basra grammarians said: It is in the accusative case, because the answer to the command is with the letter fa’, or it could be a supplication against them because they disobeyed. It has been reported that the one who said this statement used to say: It is in the accusative case, in apposition to his statement: So that they may go astray from Your path. Another of them said, and it is the saying of the grammarians of Kufa: Its position is in the subjunctive mood, based on the supplication of Moses, peace be upon them, meaning: so do not believe, as the poet said: Do not let what is hidden appear before your eyes, and do not meet me except with your nose downcast. Meaning: (May what is hidden not be spread out from between your eyes), (nor may you meet me), in the supplication. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: It is a supplication, as if he said: O God, so let them not believe. He said: If you wish, you can make it an answer to his question to him, because the question was issued in the form of a command, so you make: so let them not believe in the accusative case as an answer, and it is not easy. He said: It would be like the saying of the poet: Oh camel, go with a broad neck to Solomon, so that we may rest. He said: The answer is not in the supplication, because it is not a condition. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement about that is that it is in the place of a supplication, meaning: so do not believe. I chose that because what preceded it was a supplication, and that is His statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts. So attaching His statement: so do not believe, since it was in the context of that, to its meaning is more appropriate and more fitting. As for his saying: Until they see the painful torment, Ibn Abbas used to say that its meaning is: Until they see the drowning. We have mentioned the narration from him regarding that from some of its aspects previously. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abbas said: And they will not believe until they see the painful punishment, he said: drowning.
10:89: Abu Jaafar said: This is report from God about His answer to Moses, peace be upon him, and Aaron’s supplication against Pharaoh, the nobles of his people, and their wealth. God Almighty says: God said to them: Your supplication has been answered, against Pharaoh, his people, and their wealth. If someone says: How was the answer attributed to two people, while the supplication was only from one person? It was said: Even if the supplicant was one, the second was a believer, namely Aaron, and therefore the answer was attributed to them both, because the believer is a supplicant. And the people of interpretation said the same. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Your prayer has been answered, he said: Moses was praying, and Aaron was saying Amen, so that is what he said: Your prayer has been answered. Some Arabists have claimed that Arabs address one person as if they were two, and he recited the following about this: I said to my friend, Do not rush us to pull out its roots and cut down the wormwood. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zakariya bin Adi told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: Your prayer has been answered, he said: Moses prayed and Aaron believed. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father and Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, he said: Moses called and Aaron responded to him.... He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of his sheikh, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: Moses called and Aaron responded to him. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: Your prayer has been answered, he said: Moses prayed and Aaron believed.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, and Abd God ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, who said: Moses prayed and Aaron said, Amen, and that is what he said: Your prayer has been answered. Al-Husayn bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: “He said: Your prayer has been answered,” he said: Moses was praying and Aaron was saying: Amen, so that is what he said: Your prayer has been answered. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: Your prayer has been answered, for Moses and Aaron. Ibn Jurayj said, Ikrimah said: Aaron responded to Moses’ prayer, so God said: Your prayer has been answered, so be steadfast. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: Aaron used to say Amen, and God said: Your prayer has been answered, so the Amen became a prayer, and he became his partner in it. As for his saying: So be steadfast, it is a command from God Almighty to Moses and Aaron to be steadfast and firm in their matter, from Pharaoh’s call to answer to the oneness of God and obedience to Him, until God’s punishment comes to them, which He informed them that He answered them in, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: So be upright, meaning carry out my command, and it is uprightness. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that Pharaoh remained forty years after this call. And His statement: And do not follow the path of those who do not know, meaning: And do not take the path of those who are ignorant of the truth of My promise, so that you hasten My judgment, for My promise cannot be broken, and My threat is descending upon Pharaoh, and My punishment is inflicted upon him and his people.
10:90: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We crossed the sea with the Children of Israel until they crossed it, and Pharaoh pursued them, meaning: Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them. It is said from it, I followed him and I followed him, which have the same meaning. Al-Kisa’i, according to what Abu Ubaid mentioned about him, used to say: If it is meant that he followed them in good or evil, then the statement is ataba’ahum with a hamza on the alif. If it is meant: he followed their traces, or: he imitated them, then it is from itba’ta, with a shaddah on the ta’, without a hamza on the alif. They transgressed against Moses and Aaron and those who were with them from their people from the Children of Israel, and they were hostile, meaning: and they attacked them. It is a source of their saying: So-and-so attacked so-and-so in injustice, he attacked him aggressively, like He invaded, he invades, he invades. It was narrated that some of them used to read: Baghyan wa Adwan, which is also a source of their saying: Ada ya’du ‘udwan, like: Ala ya’lu ‘alwan. “Until drowning overtook him,” he says: until drowning surrounded him, and in the speech there is something omitted, it was omitted to mention it because of the indication of what appeared in the speech about it, and that is: So Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in oppression and aggression, in it (So We drowned him), until drowning overtook him. And His saying: He said, ‘I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims,’ God Almighty says, informing about what Pharaoh said when he was about to drown and was certain of his destruction: I believe, meaning: I acknowledge that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe. There are different readings of this: Some of them read, and this is the general reading of Medina and Basra, that he with the opening of the alif of that he with the application of I believed in it, and its accusative with it. Others read: I believed that he with a kasra on the alif of that he as the beginning of the report. This is the reading of the majority of the Kufians. Abu Jaafar said: My opinion on this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated, Yahya ibn Wadh narrated, Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: Jacob and his sons gathered with Joseph, and they were seventy-two, and they left Egypt with Moses when they left, and they were six hundred thousand. When Pharaoh caught up with them and they saw him, they said: O Moses, where is the way out? We have caught up with him, and we were suffering from Pharaoh. So God revealed to Moses: Strike the sea with your staff, and it split apart, and each part was like a great mountain, and the sea dried up for them, and God uncovered the face of the earth, and Pharaoh came out on a black horse, on his color from blackness eight hundred thousand, in addition to their colors of beasts. And under Gabriel, peace be upon him, was a thin horse, and there was no other female among them, and Michael was leading them, and no man of them deviated from it except that he added him to the people. When the last of the Children of Israel came out, Gabriel approached him and stuck to him. The horse smelled the scent of a female, but Pharaoh could not control his actions. He said: Go forward, for these people have no more right to the sea than you! Then Pharaoh pursued them, until they were the first to come out. He bumped into them and called out: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims. And it was called out: Now, although you disobeyed before and were of the corrupters. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and on the authority of `Adi ibn Thabit, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - he said: “One of them traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Gabriel used to put clay in Pharaoh’s mouth for fear that he would say: There is no god but God.” Al-Husayn bin Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, began to put - or stuff - clay into Pharaoh’s mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.” Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Katheer bin Zadhan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel said to me: O Muhammad, if you could see me covering him and putting some of the dirt in his mouth, for fear that God’s mercy would reach him and he would be forgiven! He meant Pharaoh.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God drowned Pharaoh, he said: ‘I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe.’ So Gabriel said: O Muhammad, if you saw me, I would take from the mud of the sea and put it in his mouth, for fear that mercy would reach him.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told me, on the authority of Hakam, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When Pharaoh said: ‘There is no god but God,’ Gabriel began to fill it with clay and dirt.” Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, I was told by someone who heard Maimun ibn Mihran say about His statement: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, he said: Gabriel took some of the mud of the sea and struck his mouth with it - or he said he filled his mouth with it - for fear that God’s mercy would reach him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Burqan, on the authority of Maimun ibn Mihran, he said: Ad-Dahhak ibn Qays delivered a sermon, praised God and extolled Him, then said: Pharaoh was a tyrannical slave who forgot the remembrance of God. When he was about to drown, he said: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims. God said: Now, although you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.... He said, my father told me, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of `Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Pharaoh was about to drown, Gabriel began to stuff dirt into his mouth, fearing that he would be forgiven.... He said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi: That Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: I have not envied mercy for anyone among the children of Adam except Pharaoh, for when he said what he said, I feared that it would reach the Lord and He would have mercy on him, so I took some of the mud and foam of the sea and struck his eyes and face with it.... He said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Ya`la, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: I stuffed his mouth with mud for fear that mercy would reach him.
10:91: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says, informing Pharaoh of the ugliness of his actions during his life, and his wrongdoing towards himself during his health, by his persistence in his tyranny, and his disobedience to his Lord, when he fled to Him in a state of His wrath upon him, and His punishment descending, seeking refuge in Him from His torment that was befalling him, when he called out to Him while the waves of the sea overwhelmed him, and the anguish of death overwhelmed him, I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims to Him, submitting in humility to Him, acknowledging servitude: Now, you acknowledge servitude to God, surrender to Him in humility, and devote divinity to Him, and you disobeyed Him before His vengeance descended upon you, so you angered Him against yourself, and you were among the corruptors on earth, turning people away from His path? Why don't you, while you are in a respite, and the door of repentance is open to you, acknowledge what you are acknowledging now?
10:92: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to Pharaoh: Today We will place you on a high ground with your body, and those who deny your destruction will see you as a perishing creature, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you, meaning: for those who come after you among the people, a lesson from you, so that they may be deterred from disobeying God, disbelief, and striving to spread corruption on His earth. And al-Najwa is a high place above the surrounding land. From this, Aws bin Hajar said: He who is saved by his punishment is like he who is saved by his salvation, and he who is hidden is like he who walks on a treadmill. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Salil, on the authority of Qays bin Abbad and others, he said: The Children of Israel said to Moses: Pharaoh has not died! He said: So God brought him out to them and they looked at him like a red bull. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu al-Salil, on the authority of Qays ibn Ubad, he said - and he was one of the most knowledgeable people - or: the most recent people - about the Children of Israel, he said: So he told us that when the first of Pharaoh's soldiers reached the sea, the horses feared the flames. He said: And a thin horse appeared to one of them, and he smelled its scent - I think he said: - so he slipped away and I followed him. He said: So when the last of Pharaoh's soldiers were in the sea, and the last of the Children of Israel came out, he ordered the sea to close in on them. So the Children of Israel said: Pharaoh did not die, and he would never die! So God heard their denial of His Prophet, he said: So He threw him on the shore like a red bull, and the Children of Israel could see him. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wazeh told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad: So today We will save you with your body, he said: (His body), his body, the sea threw him into it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So today We will save you with your body, he said: with your body. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Al-Asbagh bin Zaid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, he said: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When Moses crossed the sea with all those with him, the sea met them - meaning: Pharaoh and his people - and drowned them. Moses’ companions said: We fear that Pharaoh has not drowned, and we do not believe in his destruction. So he called upon his Lord, and He brought him out, and the sea cast him out, until they were certain of his destruction. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So today We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you, he said: Groups of the Children of Israel denied that, so God threw him on the shore of the sea for them to look at. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So that it may be a sign for those who come after you, he said: When God drowned Pharaoh, a group of people did not believe that, so God brought him out as a sign and a sermon. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Salil, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, or someone else, similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Muammar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid: So today We will save you with your body, he said: with your body.... He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, I was told on the authority of Mujahid: So today We will save you with your body, he said: with your body. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: The Children of Israel denied the death of Pharaoh, so he threw him on the shore of the sea for the Children of Israel to see. He said: Red, like a bull. Others said: You will save your body from the sea, so we will take it out of it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: So today We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you, meaning that God saved Pharaoh for the Children of Israel from the sea, and they looked at him after he had drowned. If someone says: What is the meaning of his saying: With your body? Is it permissible for him to be saved with something other than his body, so that the statement requires that it be said in it: With your body? It was said: It was permissible for him to save him with his body alive as he entered the sea. Since that was permissible, it was said: So today We will save you with your body, so that it would be known that He would save him with the body without a soul, but dead. And His statement: And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, God Almighty says: And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, meaning: of Our arguments and evidence that worship and divinity are exclusively for Us, are heedless, meaning: forgetful, they do not reflect on them, nor do they consider them.
10:93: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And We settled the Children of Israel in true dwellings. It was said: He meant by that the Levant and Jerusalem. It was said: He meant the Levant and Egypt. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: A place of truth, he said: The places of truth, Egypt and the Levant. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A place of truth, he said, God made them dwell in the Levant and Jerusalem. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in a place of truth, Ash-Sham: And he read: To the land which We had blessed for the worlds (Al-Anbiya’: 71). And His saying: And We provided them with good things, means: And We provided the Children of Israel with lawful sustenance, which is good. And His statement: And they did not differ until knowledge came to them, God Almighty says: And these children of Israel to whom We did this action did not differ until what they knew came to them. That is because before the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they were unanimous in the prophethood of Muhammad and in acknowledging him and his mission, not differing about him in the description that they found written with them. But when what they knew came to them, some of them disbelieved in it and some of them believed in it, and the believers in it among them were a small number. So that is His statement: And they did not differ until what was known came to them, whom they knew, a prophet of God, so He put knowledge in place of the known. Some of them interpreted knowledge here as the Book of God and His revelation. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: And they did not differ until knowledge came to them, he said: Knowledge is the Book of God that He revealed, and His command that He commanded them with. Did they differ until knowledge came to them out of envy among themselves? The people of these desires, did they fight except for envy! He said: Envy has two aspects: the aspect of preciousness in this world and those of its people who fought over it, and envy in knowledge, seeing this one as ignorant and mistaken, and seeing himself as correct and knowledgeable, so he envies this one who is mistaken with his accuracy and knowledge. And His statement: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, will judge between those of the Children of Israel who differed concerning you on the Day of Resurrection, concerning that over which they used to differ concerning My affair in this world, by admitting those of them who disbelieved in you into Hell, and those of them who believed in you into Paradise. So that is His judgment on that day concerning that over which they used to differ concerning the affair of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:94: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you, O Muhammad, are in doubt about the truth of what We have chosen you for and revealed to you, that the Children of Israel did not differ about your prophethood before you were sent as a Messenger to His creation, because they find you written down among them, and they know you by the description with which you are described in their book in the Torah and the Gospel, So ask those who read the Scripture before you, from the people of the Torah and the Gospel, such as Abdullah bin Salam and others like him, from the people of truth and faith in you among them, not the people of lies and disbelief in you among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said regarding His statement: So ask those who read the Scripture before you, he said: The Torah and the Gospel, those who met Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Scripture and believed in him. He says: So ask them if you are in doubt that you are written among them. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam, he was one of the People of the Scripture. So he believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: So ask those who read the Scripture before you, he said: They are the People of the Scripture. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: So ask those who read the Scripture before you, meaning the people of piety and faith from among the People of the Scripture, who were at the time of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If someone were to say: Was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in doubt that the report of God was the certain truth, to the point that it was said to him: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Scripture before you? It was said: No, and this is what a group of scholars said. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt and did not ask. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he said: He did not doubt and he did not ask. Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, and Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding this verse, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt and did not ask. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt and I do not ask. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Scripture before you, he said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt and I do not ask. If he said: What is the way to explain this statement, then, if the matter is as you described? It was said: We have explained in more than one place in this book of ours that the Arabs permitted the saying of one of them to his slave: (If you are my slave, then submit to my command), and the slave who is commanded to do so does not doubt that his master who said that to him is his slave. Likewise, the saying of one of them to his son: (If you are my son, then be dutiful to me), and he does not doubt that his son is his son, and that this is from their speech that is correct and widespread among them, and we mentioned that with its evidence, and from it is the saying of God: {And when God said, O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, Take me and my mother as gods besides God} (al-Ma’idah 5:116), and God, the Most High, knew that Jesus did not say that. This is from that, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt the truth of God’s report and its correctness, and God, the Most High, reminded him of that from His command, and He was aware, but He, the Most High, addressed him as his people addressed one another, since the Qur’an was revealed in their language. As for his saying: The truth has come to you from your Lord verse, it is a statement from God that is the subject. God Almighty says: I swear that the certain truth has come to you from the report that you are a Messenger of God, and that these Jews and Christians know the truth of that, and they find your description in their books, So do not be among those who doubt, meaning: So do not be among those who doubt the truth of that. If someone were to say: This verse was addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is some of those who did not have sound insight into his prophethood, may God bless him and grant him peace, but who had shown faith with their tongues, alerting them to a place where they could know the truth of his matter, which would remove confusion from their hearts, as God Almighty said: “O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.” (al-Ahzab 33:1), it would be a statement whose validity is not proven.
10:95: Abu Ja`far said: And God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not be, O Muhammad, among those who denied God’s proofs and evidence, lest you be among those who lost their fortune and sold God’s mercy and pleasure for His wrath and punishment.
10:96: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Those upon whom the word of your Lord is incumbent, O Muhammad, is His curse upon them by His saying: Indeed, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers (Hud 11:18), so it was confirmed upon them. It is said: So-and-so has a right to such-and-such, if it is proven and obligatory for him. And His saying: They will not believe, even if every sign came to them, means: They will not believe in God’s proofs, nor will they acknowledge the Oneness of their Lord, nor that you are God’s Messenger.
10:97: And if every sign came to them, and admonition and lesson, and they witnessed it, until they witnessed the painful torment, just as Pharaoh and his chiefs did not believe when the word of your Lord came into effect upon them until they witnessed the painful torment, then he said: I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe (Yunus 10:90), when his words did not benefit him, so likewise those upon whom the word of your Lord came into effect from among your people, from the idol worshippers and others, they will not believe in you and follow you, except at the time when their belief will not benefit them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, he said: The wrath of God has come into effect upon them because they disobeyed Him. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, God’s wrath has come into effect upon them because they disobeyed Him.
10:98: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Why was there not a city that believed? It is also mentioned in Abi’s reading. The meaning of the words: There was no village that believed when it witnessed the punishment and the descent of God’s wrath upon it, due to its disobedience to its Lord and its deserving of His punishment, and its faith benefited it at that time, just as Pharaoh’s faith did not benefit him when he was drowned after he persisted in his transgression and deserved God’s wrath due to his disobedience, except the people of Jonah, for their faith benefited them after the punishment descended and the wrath descended upon them. So God excluded the people of Jonah from the people of the villages whose faith did not benefit them after the punishment descended upon their courtyards, and He took them out of them, and He informed His creation that their faith benefited them in particular from among all the nations other than them. If someone were to say: If the matter is as you have described, that his statement: Why was there not a village that believed and its belief benefited it, means: Why was there not a village that believed, meaning denial, then how is a people in the accusative case, when you know that what comes before the exception is denial, what comes after it is in the nominative case, and that the correct speech of the Arabs is: No one stood up except your brother and No one went out except your father? It was said: That is what is like that, if what comes after the exception is of the same type as what comes before it, and that is because (brother) is of the same type as (father), but if the two types differ so that what comes after the exception is not of the same type as what comes before it, then the eloquent of their speech is the accusative, and that is if you say: (No one remains in the house except the peg), and (We have no one except a dog or a donkey), because (the dog), (the peg) and (the donkey) are not of the same type as (one), and from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani: I couldn't find an answer, and no one is here Then he said: Except that I hide it for no reason, and distance is like a pool that sheds light on the oppressed. So (al-Awari) was placed in the accusative case, since it was an exception from something other than its own kind. Likewise, (the people of Yunus) was placed in the accusative case, because they are a nation other than the nations from which they were excepted, and other than their kind and form, even though they were from the children of Adam. This exception, which some Arab scholars call the discontinuous exception, had (the people of Yunus) been part of (the nation) from which they were excepted, the statement would have been in the nominative case, but they are as described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it? He said: There was no town that believed and its faith benefited it when the punishment of God descended upon it, except the town of Yunus. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: There was no town that believed and its faith benefited it, as the faith of the people of Yunus benefited from it, except the people of Yunus. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time,” he says: This did not happen among the nations before them. It did not benefit a city that disbelieved and then believed when the punishment was about to come to it, and then it was left, except the people of Jonah. When they lost their prophet and thought that the punishment had drawn near to them, God cast repentance into their hearts, and they put on sackcloth, and separated every animal from its young, then they cried out to God for forty nights. So when God knew the sincerity in their hearts, and the repentance and regret for what had happened from them, God removed from them the punishment after it had descended upon them. He said: It was mentioned to us that the people of Jonah were in Nineveh, the land of Mosul. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Except the people of Yunus, he said: It reached us that they went out and camped on a hill, and separated every animal from its young, calling upon God for forty nights, until He accepted their repentance. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdul Hamid Al-Hamani told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The torment covered the people of Yunus, just as a garment covers a grave. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The punishment descended upon the people of Yunus until there was only two-thirds of a mile between them and it. When they called out, God removed it from them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Ishaq said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus, when they believed, he said: As the people of Yunus benefited, Abu Hudhayfah added in his hadith, he said: There was not a city that believed when it saw the punishment and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus, we gave them enjoyment. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi bin Anas, he said, a man who had recited the Qur’an in his heart, during the caliphate of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, told us about the people of Yunus when he warned his people and they denied him, so he told them that the punishment would befall them, and he left them. So when they saw that and the punishment overtook them, they left their homes and ascended to a high place, and that they cried out to their Lord and called upon Him, sincerely devoting their religion to Him: that He would remove the punishment from them and that their Messenger would return to them. He said: So about that, the verse was revealed: “Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.” So there was no city that was overtaken by the punishment and then held back, except the people of Yunus in particular. When Yunus saw that, he went away blaming his Lord, and he set off in anger, thinking that He would not prevail over him, until he boarded a ship, and its people were struck by a strong wind, so he mentioned the story of Yunus and his report. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said: When they felt the punishment was about to descend, they separated every female and her child from among the people and the livestock, then they all stood up and called upon God and made their faith sincere, and they saw the punishment being lifted from them. When the punishment was lifted from them, Yunus said: Go back to them, for you have lied to them! Yunus had promised them the punishment on a third morning, so at that moment he went out angry, and his opinion was bad. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: When Yunus was sent to his people, calling them to Islam, and he abandoned what they were doing, he said: He called them, but they refused. So it was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come to them in the morning. They said: We have not found him lying, so look, if he spends the night among you, then he is nothing, and if he does not spend the night, then know that the punishment will come to you in the morning. So when it was the dead of night, he took three bags and took some provisions from them, then he went out. When morning came, the punishment covered them, as a man is covered by a garment in the grave. So they separated a man from his child, and an animal from its child. Then they cried out to God and said: We believe in what Yunus brought, and we have spoken the truth! So God removed the punishment from them. Yunus went out to look at the punishment, but he did not see anything. He said: They have found me lying! So he went, angry with his Lord, until he reached the sea. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, who said: Ibn Masoud narrated to us regarding the treasury, he said: Yunus, peace be upon him, had promised his people punishment, and he informed them that it would come to them in three days, so they separated every mother from her child, then they went out and cried out to God and asked His forgiveness. So God withheld the punishment from them, and Yunus went to see the punishment but did not see anything. And whoever lied and had no evidence was killed, so he went away in anger. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Salih al-Mari told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, on the authority of Abu al-Jild Jilan, who said: When the torment overtook the people of Yunus, they went to an old man from among the remaining scholars of theirs and said to him: The torment has descended upon us, so what do you think? He said: Say: O Ever-Living when there is no living, O Ever-Living, the Reviver of the dead, O Ever-Living, there is no god but You! So the torment was removed from them, and they enjoyed themselves for a time. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: I heard in the letter of Ibn Masoud: Fulaula, meaning: Why not? And His statement: When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, meaning: When they believed in their Messenger and acknowledged what he brought to them, after the punishment had overshadowed them and the command of God had enveloped them and the affliction had descended upon them, We removed from them the punishment of humiliation and disgrace in their life of this world, and We gave them enjoyment for a time, meaning: We delayed their appointed times and did not hasten their punishment, and We left them in this world enjoying their appointed times until the time of their death and the time of the end of their lives, which We had decreed to end.
10:99: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And if He had willed, O Muhammad, your Lord would have believed, all those on earth would have believed, in you, so they would have believed that you are My Messenger, and that what you have brought and what you are calling them to of the Oneness of God and sincere worship of Him, is true, but He does not will that, because it was decreed by God before He sent you as a Messenger that no one would believe in you, nor follow you and believe in what God sent you with of guidance and light, except for those for whom happiness was previously decreed in the first Book before the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them were created. And these are the ones who marvel at the truth of Our revelation to you of this Qur'an so that you may warn with it those whom I have commanded you to warn, from those who have already been decreed by Me that they will not believe in you in the previous Book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together, “And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God,” (Yunus 10:100), and something similar to this in the Qur’an, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was keen for all people to believe and follow him in guidance, so God informed him that no one believes except he for whom God has predestined happiness in the first mention, and no one goes astray except he for whom God has predestined misery in the first mention. If someone says: What is the point of his saying: All of those on earth will believe, since all indicates all, and all indicates all, so what is the point of repeating that, and each one of them is sufficient for the other? It was said: The Arabs differed on this: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He used the phrase both in this place as an emphasis, just as he said: Do not take two gods (al-Nahl 16:51). So in his phrase two gods is evidence of two. Another said: He came with his saying: all together after all of them, because all together only occurs as an emphasis, and all of them occurs as an emphasis and a noun, so he came with all together after all of them. He said: If it was said that he combined them to show that their meaning is one, it would be permissible here. He said: Likewise: two gods (al-Nahl 16:51), the whole number is explained by it, so it is said: (I saw four people), so when he came with (two), and the number was sufficient from it, because they say: (I have one dirham and two dirhams), it is sufficient from their saying: (I have one dirham, and two dirhams), so if they said: (dirhams), they said: (three), because the plural is ambiguous, and (one) and (two) are not ambiguous, then the singular and dual were built on the structure of what is in the plural. Because it should be with each one, because (a dirham) indicates the type of which it is from, and (one) indicates all types. Likewise (two) indicate all types, and (two dirhams) indicate themselves, so it came with numbers, because it is the origin. And His saying: Would you then compel the people until they become believers? God Almighty is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: No one will believe you, O Muhammad, and no one will follow you and acknowledge what you have brought except those whom your Lord wills to believe in you, not because you forced them, nor because you were keen on that. Would you then compel the people until they become believers in you, believing in what you have brought them from your Lord? God Almighty is saying to him: So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect that they will not believe.
10:100: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet: There is no way for a soul that You created to believe in you, O Muhammad, except by giving it permission to do so. So do not exhaust yourself in seeking its guidance, and convey to it the threat of God, and make it know what your Lord has commanded you to make it know, then leave it, for its guidance is in the hand of its Creator. Al-Thawri used to say in his interpretation of his saying: Except by the permission of God, what: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God, he said: By the decree of God. As for His statement: And He places defilement upon those who do not reason, then the Most High says: Indeed, God guides whomever He wills of His creation to believe in you, O Muhammad, and He gives him permission to believe in you, so he believes in you, follows you, and acknowledges what you have brought from your Lord. And He places defilement, which is the torment and wrath of God, upon those who do not reason, meaning: those who do not understand from God His arguments, sermons, and signs by which He, the Most High, indicated the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of what he called them to of the oneness of God and the rejection of rivals and idols. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And He makes the unclean, he said: wrath.
10:101: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people, who ask you for signs to prove the truth of what you are calling them to of the Oneness of God and the abandonment of rivals and idols: Look, O people, what signs are in the heavens that indicate the truth of what I am calling you to of the Oneness of God, from its sun and moon, and the alternation of its night and day, and the rain descending with provisions for the servants from its clouds, and in the earth from its ropes, and its cracking with its plants and the sustenance of its people, and all kinds of its wonders, for in that for you, if you understand and ponder, is a lesson and a lesson and an indication that this is from the actions of the One who cannot have a partner in His kingdom, nor does He have a back for His management and preservation, which suffices you from other signs. God Almighty says: And what do the signs and warnings avail a people who do not believe? God Almighty says: And what do the arguments, lessons, and messengers warning the servants of God against His punishment avail a people for whom God has already decreed misery, and for whom He has decreed in the Mother of the Book that they are among the people of the Fire? They do not believe in any of that nor do they affirm it, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment.
10:102: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, warning the polytheists of his people of the imminent arrival of His punishment upon them, similar to what happened to their counterparts before them from all the nations that came before them, who followed the path of denying the Messengers of God and rejecting the Oneness of their Lord: Do these polytheists of your people, who deny what you have brought them from God, await, O Muhammad, anything but a day when they will witness from God’s punishment the same as the days of their ancestors who were upon the same polytheism and denial that they are upon, who passed before them and passed away from the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud? Say to them, O Muhammad, if they are awaiting that: then await God’s punishment upon you, and the descent of His wrath upon you, for I am among those awaiting your destruction and ruin by the punishment that will befall you from God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? He says: God’s events with those who passed on before them, the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, regarding His statement: Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? Say, “Then wait, indeed, I am with you among those who wait. He said: He frightened them with His punishment, vengeance, and chastisement, then He informed them that if something like that happened, God would save His messengers and those who believed with him, so God said: “Then We will save Our messengers and those who believed. Thus is it incumbent upon Us to save the believers.”
10:103: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from your al-Nas 114:Wait for a time like the days of those who passed away before you from the previous nations who were destroyed by the punishment of God, for when that comes, no one will be destroyed by it except them and those who were like them in denying you, then We will save there Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed in him and confirmed his truth and followed his religion, just as We did before that with Our messengers whose nations We destroyed, so We saved them and those who believed in him with them from Our punishment when it was due upon their nations, Thus it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers, meaning: Just as We did with the previous ones from Our messengers, so We saved them and the believers with them and destroyed their nations, so We will do with you, O Muhammad, and with the believers, so We will save you and save the believers with you, incumbent upon Us without a doubt.
10:104: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people who are amazed that I have revealed to you: If you are in doubt, O people, about my religion to which I call you, and you do not know that it is the truth from God, then I do not worship those you worship besides God, of the gods and idols that do not hear or see and do not avail me at all, so that you doubt its authenticity. This is an insinuation and a subtle tone of speech, but the meaning of the speech is: If you are in doubt about my religion, then you should not doubt it, but you should doubt what you are doing, which is the worship of idols that do not understand anything, and do not harm or benefit. As for my religion, you should not doubt it, because I worship God, who takes the creation and causes them to die if He wills, and benefits them and harms them if He wills. That is because the worship of one who is like this is not denounced by anyone with a sound nature. As for the worship of idols, every person with a sound mind and intellect denounces it. And His saying: But I worship God who takes your souls, meaning: But I worship God who takes your souls and causes you to die at your appointed times. And I have been commanded to be among the believers, meaning: He is the One who commanded me to be among those who believe in what came to me from Him.
10:105: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And I was commanded to be among the believers, “and to establish,” and the second that is in apposition to the first that. What he means by his saying: Set your face toward the religion, is to set yourself upon the religion of Islam, upright in it, not deviating from it to Judaism or Christianity, or idol worship. And do not be among those who associate others with God, meaning: Do not be among those who associate others with God in the worship of their Lord, lest you be among those who are destroyed.
10:106: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And do not, O Muhammad, invoke, besides your God and Creator, anything that will not benefit you in this world or in the Hereafter, nor harm you in religion or in this world, meaning by that the gods and idols. He says: Do not worship them hoping for their benefit or fearing their harm, for they neither benefit nor harm. If you do, that, and invoke them besides God, then you will be among the wrongdoers, meaning: among those who associate partners with God and wrong themselves.
10:107: Abu Ja'far said: The Almighty says to His Prophet: And if God afflicts you, O Muhammad, with hardship or affliction, there is none who can remove that except your Lord who afflicted you with it, not what these polytheists worship of gods and rivals, And if He intends for you good, meaning: And if He intends for you ease or blessing and well-being and joy, there is none who can repel His favor, meaning: No one can stand between you and that, nor prevent you from it, nor deprive you of it, because He is the One in whose hand is ease and hardship, not the gods and idols, nor anything else, He afflicts with it whom He wills, meaning: Your Lord afflicts, O Muhammad, with ease and affliction, ease and hardship, whomever He wills and desires, of His servants, and He is the Forgiving, of the sins of those of His servants who repent and return from their disbelief and polytheism to faith in Him and obedience to Him, the Merciful, of those of them who believe in Him and obey Him, that He does not punish them after their repentance and return.
10:108: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to the people, O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, meaning: the Book of God, in which is an explanation of everything that people need in their religious affairs, So whoever is guided, meaning: whoever is upright and follows the path of truth, and believes in what came from God of explanation, is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, meaning: he is upright on guidance and follows the path for himself, so he seeks good for himself by doing that and no one else, And whoever goes astray, meaning: whoever deviates from the truth that came to him from God, and contradicts his religion and what he was sent with Muhammad and the Book that he revealed to him, is only led astray to his own detriment, meaning: for the misguidance of that person only brings upon himself, not upon others, because no one else is held accountable for that, and no one will be led to destruction by that misguidance except himself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, And I am not a guardian over you. He says: I have no authority over you to straighten you out. Your affair is up to God, and He is the One who straightens whomever He wills among you. I am only a messenger conveying to you what I was sent to you with.
10:109: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And follow, O Muhammad, the revelation of God that He reveals to you, and His revelation that He sends down to you, so act according to it, and be patient with what befalls you in God's cause from the polytheists of your people of harm and hardships, and with what befalls you from them, until God decides His matter concerning them and you with a decisive action, And He is the best of judges, meaning: He is the best of judges and the most just of judges. So God Almighty judged between him and them on the day of Badr, and killed them with the sword, and He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, concerning those who remained of them to take the path of those of them who were destroyed, or to repent and return to His obedience, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: “And I am not a guardian over you. And follow what is revealed to you and be patient until God decides, and He is the best of judges,” he said: This is abrogated, until God decides, God’s judgment is to fight them, and His command to be harsh with them. The last interpretation of Surah Yunus, peace be upon him
